questionText: Which term describes a system's ability to remain operational and accessible without interruption even when individual components fail?

options.label: A
options.text: High Availability (HA)

options.label: B
options.text: Economies of scale

options.label: C
options.text: Capital expenditure

options.label: D
options.text: Stateless filtering

explanation: High Availability ensures that an application or service remains continuously operational and accessible with minimal downtime.

questionText: What is the primary difference between High Availability (HA) and Fault Tolerance (FT)?

options.label: A
options.text: High Availability minimizes downtime; Fault Tolerance achieves zero downtime by operating through component failures with built-in redundancy

options.label: B
options.text: Fault tolerance requires cloud computing, whereas HA only works on-premises

options.label: C
options.text: HA guarantees zero data loss; fault tolerance guarantees nothing

options.label: D
options.text: They are identical concepts with no technical distinction

explanation: Fault tolerance ensures zero disruption through full redundancy (often at higher cost), whereas high availability aims for minimal downtime.

questionText: Which architectural principle is demonstrated by distributing Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones (Multi-AZ)?

options.label: A
options.text: High Availability and Fault Tolerance

options.label: B
options.text: Single point of failure

options.label: C
options.text: Vertical scaling

options.label: D
options.text: Consolidated billing

explanation: Multi-AZ deployment ensures that if one Availability Zone encounters power or network issues, healthy instances in other AZs continue handling traffic.

questionText: Which type of scaling involves adding more power, CPU, or RAM to an existing virtual server (e.g., upgrading from t3.small to m5.2xlarge)?

options.label: A
options.text: Vertical scaling (scaling up)

options.label: B
options.text: Horizontal scaling (scaling out)

options.label: C
options.text: Predictive elasticity

options.label: D
options.text: Multi-region replication

explanation: Vertical scaling (scale up) increases the capacity of an individual instance by upgrading its instance type/size.

questionText: Which type of scaling involves adding more instances of the same size to distribute load across a fleet of servers?

options.label: A
options.text: Horizontal scaling (scaling out)

options.label: B
options.text: Vertical scaling (scaling up)

options.label: C
options.text: Diagonal scaling

options.label: D
options.text: Ephemeral scaling

explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds more parallel instances to handle increased traffic, which is a foundational best practice in cloud architectures.

questionText: What is Recovery Time Objective (RTO) in disaster recovery planning?

options.label: A
options.text: The maximum acceptable duration of time that an application can be down after a disaster before service is restored

options.label: B
options.text: The maximum age of files that must be recovered from backup storage for normal operations to resume

options.label: C
options.text: The total monetary cost of restoring servers

options.label: D
options.text: The time required to purchase new physical servers

explanation: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the target time allowed between system disruption and full restoration of service.

questionText: What is Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in disaster recovery planning?

options.label: A
options.text: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time (e.g., 15 minutes of lost transactions)

options.label: B
options.text: The time it takes to boot an operating system

options.label: C
options.text: The physical GPS coordinates of a disaster recovery site

options.label: D
options.text: The maximum network latency between two regions

explanation: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) measures the maximum acceptable time window of potential data loss due to a disaster.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy has the lowest cost but the highest Recovery Time Objective (RTO)?

options.label: A
options.text: Backup and Restore

options.label: B
options.text: Pilot Light

options.label: C
options.text: Warm Standby

options.label: D
options.text: Multi-Site Active-Active

explanation: Backup and Restore stores data backups in services like Amazon S3 and reconstructs infrastructure only after a disaster strikes, taking hours to restore.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy maintains a minimal, scaled-down version of core infrastructure running continuously in a secondary region that can be scaled up rapidly during a disaster?

options.label: A
options.text: Warm Standby

options.label: B
options.text: Backup and Restore

options.label: C
options.text: Cold Site

options.label: D
options.text: Offline archival

explanation: Warm Standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the environment in the DR region that can quickly scale up to full production capacity.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy keeps critical core components (such as live replicated databases) running in a secondary region while compute instances remain stopped or unprovisioned until failover?

options.label: A
options.text: Pilot Light

options.label: B
options.text: Multi-Site Active-Active

options.label: C
options.text: Backup and Restore

options.label: D
options.text: Tape backup

explanation: In a Pilot Light strategy, core data systems are continuously synchronized (the 'pilot light' burns), while web/app servers are provisioned only during a disaster.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy offers near-zero RTO and near-zero RPO, but comes with the highest ongoing infrastructure cost?

options.label: A
options.text: Multi-Site Active-Active

options.label: B
options.text: Warm Standby

options.label: C
options.text: Pilot Light

options.label: D
options.text: Backup and Restore

explanation: Multi-Site Active-Active serves production traffic from two or more regions simultaneously. If one fails, traffic shifts instantly with near-zero data loss.

questionText: An architecture replaces a single massive database server with an Amazon Aurora cluster containing one primary write instance and three read replicas across three Availability Zones. What does this achieve?

options.label: A
options.text: Eliminates single points of failure and improves read scalability and availability

options.label: B
options.text: Increases write latency by 500%

options.label: C
options.text: Removes the need for database user authentication

options.label: D
options.text: Restricts database queries to internal private subnets only

explanation: Distributing replicas across multiple AZs removes single points of failure, allows automatic failover, and scales read query capacity.

questionText: Which of the following is an anti-pattern when designing for high availability in the cloud?

options.label: A
options.text: Hosting all web, application, and database components on a single standalone EC2 instance in one Availability Zone

options.label: B
options.text: Deploying an Application Load Balancer across multiple subnets in different AZs

options.label: C
options.text: Utilizing Amazon S3 for durable object storage across multiple facilities

options.label: D
options.text: Implementing stateless web servers managed by an Auto Scaling group

explanation: Putting all layers on a single instance in a single AZ creates a severe single point of failure (SPOF) with zero redundancy.

questionText: How does loose coupling between microservices improve system reliability?

options.label: A
options.text: It prevents a failure in one service from cascading and bringing down the entire application

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees that software developers never need to write documentation

options.label: C
options.text: It eliminates the need for network security firewalls

options.label: D
options.text: It forces all microservices to use the same database tables

explanation: Loose coupling (e.g., using Amazon SQS message queues between components) isolates services so that if downstream services pause or fail, upstream services continue operating.

questionText: What role does Amazon Route 53 play in a multi-region disaster recovery architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: It performs DNS health checks and automatically routes traffic away from an unhealthy region to a healthy backup region

options.label: B
options.text: It physically repairs damaged fiber optic lines

options.label: C
options.text: It replicates relational database tables between regions

options.label: D
options.text: It converts SQL databases into NoSQL tables automatically

explanation: Amazon Route 53 provides DNS failover routing, monitoring endpoint health and rerouting user requests to a standby region if the primary region becomes unavailable.

questionText: What are two key characteristics of stateless application design in AWS? Select TWO.

options.label: A
options.text: User session state is stored outside the web instance (e.g., in Amazon ElastiCache or DynamoDB)

options.label: B
options.text: Any individual web server instance can be terminated or replaced without impacting the user experience

options.label: C
options.text: All user files are stored exclusively on the instance's ephemeral root drive

options.label: D
options.text: Instances must run continuously for at least 3 years without restarting

options.label: E
options.text: The application cannot communicate with any external databases

explanation: Stateless design offloads session data to external stores (DynamoDB/ElastiCache), allowing instances to scale out or be terminated gracefully at any moment.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy provides the best balance of low cost and fast recovery for non-critical enterprise applications?

options.label: A
options.text: Pilot Light

options.label: B
options.text: Multi-Site Active-Active

options.label: C
options.text: Manual tape shipping

options.label: D
options.text: Single-AZ standalone instance

explanation: Pilot Light keeps baseline data synced while compute remains unprovisioned, saving money while allowing recovery in tens of minutes.

questionText: What is meant by the design principle 'Design for failure and nothing will fail'?

options.label: A
options.text: Assume hardware and network disruptions will inevitably happen, and architect automated recovery mechanisms into every layer

options.label: B
options.text: Intentionally write defective software code to test employee response times

options.label: C
options.text: Purchase insurance policies instead of configuring redundant systems

options.label: D
options.text: Only run applications during working office hours

explanation: In cloud architectures, hardware components inevitably fail; designing redundant, self-healing systems ensures that individual failures never cause customer-visible outages.

questionText: Which AWS service enables automated horizontal scaling of EC2 instances based on CloudWatch metrics like CPU utilization or request count?

options.label: A

options.text: AWS Artifact

options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.text: AWS Budgets

questionText: Why is horizontal scaling generally preferred over vertical scaling in modern cloud applications?

options.label: A
options.text: Horizontal scaling allows unlimited linear expansion and eliminates single points of failure; vertical scaling has hardware ceiling limits and requires downtime to resize

options.label: B
options.text: Horizontal scaling is only compatible with Windows servers

options.label: C
options.text: Vertical scaling requires writing code in assembly language

options.label: D
options.text: Horizontal scaling prevents the use of load balancers

explanation: Upgrading an instance vertically hits physical hardware limits and often requires stopping the instance, whereas horizontal scaling adds instances dynamically without downtime.

questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy would a critical global banking transaction engine most likely implement?

options.label: A
options.text: Multi-Site Active-Active

options.label: B
options.text: Backup and Restore

options.label: C
options.text: Pilot Light

options.label: D
options.text: Cold Standby

questionText: Which AWS service decouples asynchronous components of an application by serving as a durable message queue?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs

options.label: C
options.text: AWS CloudTrail

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

questionText: An e-commerce app experiences checkout delays because order processing is synchronous with payment capture. How can loose coupling solve this?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Upgrade the web server to an accelerated computing GPU instance

options.label: C
options.text: Delete database indexes to speed up query response

options.label: D
options.text: Restrict shoppers to one item per checkout cart

explanation: Queueing orders in SQS allows the web tier to acknowledge orders immediately, decoupling front-end checkout from backend payment processing.

questionText: What is an Availability Zone (AZ) in the AWS global infrastructure?

options.label: A

options.text: A single physical server rack located in a customer's corporate office

options.label: C
options.text: A regional software firewall rule

options.label: D
options.text: A temporary storage cache located in an internet service provider office

explanation: An Availability Zone consists of one or more physical data centers within a Region, separated by meaningful distance to ensure independent fault domains.

questionText: If an enterprise has an RPO of 15 minutes, what does this require of their backup strategy?

options.label: A

options.text: Servers must be fully rebooted every 15 minutes

options.label: C
options.text: Users must change their passwords every 15 minutes

options.label: D
options.text: All employees must log off every 15 minutes

explanation: An RPO of 15 minutes means the organization can tolerate losing at most 15 minutes of data, so data must be backed up or synced at intervals no longer than 15 minutes.

questionText: Which cloud architectural practice prevents a system from becoming brittle when dependencies undergo maintenance?

options.label: A
options.text: Loose coupling through message queues, load balancers, and decoupled APIs

options.label: B
options.text: Hard-coding IP addresses directly into client application code

options.label: C
options.text: Co-locating all microservices inside a single executable binary

options.label: D
options.text: Disabling retry logic and circuit breakers

explanation: Loose coupling prevents tight interdependencies, allowing services to degrade gracefully and retry without breaking the entire architecture.

questionText: How many pillars are included in the official AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: 6 pillars

options.label: B
options.text: 4 pillars

options.label: C
options.text: 5 pillars

options.label: D
options.text: 8 pillars

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on running workloads effectively, gaining insight into operations, and continuously improving supporting processes?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Security

options.label: C
options.text: Reliability

options.label: D
options.text: Performance Efficiency

explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on executing workloads, automating changes, responding to operational events, and defining daily standards.

questionText: Which design principle is a core part of the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Perform operations as code

options.label: B
options.text: Trade upfront capital expense for variable expense

options.label: C
options.text: Overprovision compute capacity for peak traffic

options.label: D
options.text: Avoid automating operational changes

explanation: 'Perform operations as code' means defining entire infrastructure and operational procedures as software code (e.g. AWS CloudFormation) to ensure consistency.

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on protecting information, data, and systems while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies?

options.label: A
options.text: Security

options.label: B
options.text: Operational Excellence

options.label: C
options.text: Cost Optimization

options.label: D
options.text: Sustainability

explanation: The Security pillar encompasses confidentiality and integrity of data, managing user permissions, and establishing controls to detect security events.

questionText: Which design principle aligns with the Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply security at all layers (defense in depth)

options.label: B
options.text: Use a single shared password across all administrative accounts

options.label: C
options.text: Store customer passwords in plaintext in public S3 buckets

options.label: D
options.text: Disable logging to minimize storage costs

explanation: 'Apply security at all layers' advocates for defense-in-depth security across edge networks, VPCs, subnets, load balancers, compute instances, and storage.

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on ensuring a workload performs its intended function correctly and consistently when expected to do so, including recovering from infrastructure failures?

options.label: A
options.text: Reliability

options.label: B
options.text: Sustainability

options.label: C
options.text: Cost Optimization

options.label: D
options.text: Performance Efficiency

explanation: The Reliability pillar covers workload ability to withstand component failures, dynamically acquire computing resources to meet demand, and mitigate disruptions.

questionText: Which design principle belongs to the Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Automatically recover from failure

options.label: B
options.text: Keep people away from data

options.label: C
options.text: Democratize advanced technologies

options.label: D
options.text: Adopt a consumption model

explanation: 'Automatically recover from failure' means monitoring systems for degradation and triggering automated remediation (e.g., auto-scaling replacement instances).

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve?

options.label: A
options.text: Performance Efficiency

options.label: B
options.text: Security

options.label: C
options.text: Cost Optimization

options.label: D
options.text: Operational Excellence

explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on selecting the right resource types and sizes, monitoring performance, and taking advantage of cloud innovations.

questionText: Which design principle belongs to the Performance Efficiency pillar?

options.label: A
options.text: Democratize advanced technologies (delegate complex technologies to cloud vendor managed services)

options.label: B
options.text: Perform operations as code

options.label: C
options.text: Enable traceability

options.label: D
options.text: Test recovery procedures

explanation: 'Democratize advanced technologies' enables teams to adopt complex capabilities (like machine learning, media transcoding, or distributed databases) simply by consuming cloud services.

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs and running systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point?

options.label: A
options.text: Cost Optimization

options.label: B
options.text: Performance Efficiency

options.label: C
options.text: Operational Excellence

options.label: D
options.text: Reliability

explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on understanding spending, selecting cost-effective resources, scaling elastically, and eliminating waste.

questionText: Which design principle is associated with the Cost Optimization pillar?

options.label: A
options.text: Adopt a consumption model (pay only for computing resources consumed)

options.label: B
options.text: Prepare for security events

options.label: C
options.text: Make frequent, small, reversible changes

options.label: D
options.text: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability

explanation: 'Adopt a consumption model' allows organizations to pay only for the computing resources that they require, scaling spending up or down with business demand.

questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads, with emphasis on energy consumption and efficiency?

options.label: A
options.text: Sustainability

options.label: B
options.text: Operational Excellence

options.label: C
options.text: Reliability

options.label: D
options.text: Performance Efficiency

explanation: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, maximizing resource utilization, and adopting efficient hardware and architectures to reduce carbon footprint.

questionText: Which design principle belongs to the Sustainability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Understand your impact and maximize utilization of computing resources

options.label: B
options.text: Enable traceability through audit logging

options.label: C
options.text: Test disaster recovery procedures on physical tape drives

options.label: D
options.text: Deploy identical non-production environments running 24/7

explanation: The Sustainability pillar emphasizes measuring workload environmental impact and maximizing utilization (e.g., using serverless and right-sizing) to eliminate wasted energy.

questionText: What are the six official pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? Select TWO groups that together contain all six. (Select TWO)

options.text: Operational Excellence, Security, and Reliability

options.label: E

questionText: Which design principle of the Operational Excellence pillar emphasizes learning from mistakes by holding blameless post-incident retrospectives?

options.label: A
options.text: Learn from all operational failures

options.label: B
options.text: Keep people away from data

options.text: Democratize advanced technologies

options.text: Adopt a consumption model

questionText: Under the Security pillar, what does the design principle 'Keep people away from data' advocate?

options.label: A
options.text: Use automated processing pipelines, identity policies, and tools to reduce direct human access to live data records, mitigating human error and leakage

options.text: Prevent data analysts from viewing any company dashboards

options.text: Delete all database tables after 24 hours of creation

questionText: Which Reliability design principle advocates measuring recovery mechanisms using simulated game days and intentional fault injection?

options.label: A
options.text: Test recovery procedures

options.label: B
options.text: Perform operations as code

options.text: Adopt a consumption model

options.label: D
options.text: Go global in minutes

questionText: Which AWS tool provides free architectural reviews, guidance, and evaluation of workloads against the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

questionText: Under the Performance Efficiency pillar, how does adopting serverless architectures (e.g., AWS Lambda) benefit organizations?

options.label: A
options.text: It removes the operational burden of managing and optimizing servers, allowing engineers to focus on business logic

options.label: B
options.text: It eliminates the need for internet connectivity

options.label: C
options.text: It guarantees zero cost regardless of request volume

options.label: D
options.text: It converts SQL databases to text spreadsheets

questionText: Which design principle under the Cost Optimization pillar involves analyzing where money is spent and attributing expenses to individual business units?

options.label: A
options.text: Measure overall efficiency and analyze expenditure

options.label: B
options.text: Perform operations as code

options.label: C
options.text: Apply security at all layers

options.label: D
options.text: Test recovery procedures

questionText: Under the Sustainability pillar, which practice helps minimize energy consumption in an AWS environment?

options.label: A
options.text: Decommissioning idle test environments during non-business hours and using managed serverless services

options.text: Leaving thousands of empty EC2 instances running 24/7 just in case

options.text: Using older, less efficient hardware instance generations

options.label: D
options.text: Writing code in unoptimized infinite loops

questionText: What does the Operational Excellence principle 'Make frequent, small, reversible changes' achieve?

options.label: A
options.text: It reduces blast radius of changes and allows rapid rollback if an issue occurs

options.text: It forces teams to deploy software only once every two years

options.label: C
options.text: It requires all changes to be approved by a physical committee in person

options.label: D

questionText: Which component of the AWS global infrastructure is AWS entirely responsible for securing and maintaining?

options.label: A
options.text: Regions, Availability Zones, Edge Locations, and physical network cables connecting them

options.label: B
options.text: Customer VPC route tables and subnets

options.label: C
options.text: Customer Amazon RDS database user accounts

options.label: D
options.text: Customer SSL/TLS private certificates stored on local laptops

explanation: AWS owns and secures the entire global physical infrastructure, including data centers, undersea fiber cables, and edge points of presence.

questionText: A customer configures an Amazon S3 bucket with public read access, exposing company spreadsheets. Who is responsible for this misconfiguration?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS

options.label: C
options.text: The internet service provider

options.label: D
options.text: The web browser vendor

explanation: Customers control access permissions, bucket policies, and S3 Block Public Access; configuring insecure bucket permissions is the customer's responsibility.

questionText: Which of the following is an example of 'Security IN the Cloud'?

options.label: A
options.text: Encrypting sensitive customer database fields using AWS KMS customer managed keys

options.label: B
options.text: Deploying security guards at AWS data center perimeter gates

options.label: C
options.text: Upgrading physical cooling towers at an AWS facility

options.label: D
options.text: Replacing defective memory chips in server racks

explanation: Data encryption, key management, identity access policies, and network firewall configuration are all customer responsibilities ('Security IN the Cloud').

questionText: Which of the following is an example of 'Security OF the Cloud'?

options.label: A
options.text: Disposing of decommissioned storage media according to industry standards like DoD 5220.22-M

options.label: B
options.text: Rotating IAM access keys every 90 days

options.label: C
options.text: Enabling multi-factor authentication on IAM user accounts

options.label: D
options.text: Writing IAM policies following the principle of least privilege

explanation: Physical disposal and degaussing of retired hard drives in AWS facilities is an AWS responsibility ('Security OF the Cloud').

questionText: When using Amazon DynamoDB, which task does AWS handle automatically?

options.label: A
options.text: Underlying operating system installation, software patching, and distributed storage replication

options.label: B
options.text: Determining which IAM users are allowed to read or write specific tables

options.label: C
options.text: Defining primary partition keys and sort keys for the table

options.label: D
options.text: Encrypting client-side application requests before sending them across the wire

explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL service; AWS handles OS patching, hardware, network provisioning, and multi-AZ data replication.

questionText: What are two controls that AWS and the customer share responsibility for under the Shared Responsibility Model? Select TWO.

options.label: A
options.text: Configuration management (AWS configures infrastructure devices; customer configures guest OS and applications)

options.label: B
options.text: Employee awareness and training (both train their respective personnel)

options.label: C
options.text: Physical data center environmental controls

options.label: D
options.text: Physical access badges for AWS data centers

options.label: E
options.text: Customer database schema design

explanation: Shared controls apply to both AWS and the customer; configuration management and employee training are classic examples.

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for configuring firewall rules to protect an Amazon EC2 instance from unauthorized internet traffic?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer (via Security Groups and Network ACLs)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS automated support bots

options.label: C
options.text: The operating system open-source community

options.label: D
options.text: The server chip vendor

explanation: Configuring virtual firewalls (Security Groups and NACLs) to permit or deny specific IP addresses and ports is the customer's duty.

questionText: Who is responsible for verifying that AWS physical infrastructure complies with external security standards such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2?

options.label: A
options.text: Independent third-party auditors hired by AWS

options.label: B
options.text: Individual customers touring AWS data centers in person

options.label: C
options.text: Local retail electronics stores

options.label: D
options.text: Open source volunteers

explanation: Independent third-party auditors evaluate AWS physical and operational security against global standards, publishing compliance reports in AWS Artifact.

questionText: In an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) model on AWS, what percentage of data center physical infrastructure does the customer manage?
explanation: Customers manage 0% of physical data center infrastructure in AWS; AWS manages 100% of the physical facilities, power, and hardware.
sourceModule: Module 1 - Introduction to Amazon Web Services

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which responsibility falls on the customer regarding data stored in Amazon EBS volumes?

options.label: A
options.text: Enabling encryption, setting volume permissions, and taking regular backup snapshots

options.label: B
options.text: Physically replacing spinning magnetic platters in defective hard drives

options.label: C
options.text: Maintaining cooling fluid in storage server heatsinks

options.label: D
options.text: Designing the physical storage enclosure chassis

explanation: Customers choose whether to encrypt EBS volumes, take snapshots, and attach them with appropriate OS-level permissions.

questionText: Which aspect of network security is AWS solely responsible for?

options.label: A
options.text: Protecting physical cabling, optical cross-connects, and underlying networking hardware from physical tampering

options.label: B
options.text: Defining CIDR block subnets for an Amazon VPC

options.label: C
options.text: Configuring route tables for public and private subnets

options.label: D
options.text: Managing VPN pre-shared keys

explanation: Physical cabling, routing hardware, and physical switch protection are completely managed by AWS.

questionText: When utilizing AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which part of the stack is the customer responsible for maintaining?

options.label: A
options.text: Application source code and application-level configuration settings

options.label: B
options.text: Physical server hardware replacement

options.label: C
options.text: Hypervisor kernel updates

options.label: D
options.text: Data center perimeter surveillance

explanation: Elastic Beanstalk handles provisioning and platform maintenance, leaving the customer responsible for application code and custom configurations.

questionText: Who is responsible for enabling Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on the AWS account root user?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Technical Support

options.label: C
options.text: The domain registrar

options.label: D
options.text: The credit card company

explanation: Protecting root credentials by configuring virtual or hardware MFA is an urgent, non-delegable customer responsibility.

questionText: Which statement is true regarding operating system updates for Amazon RDS versus Amazon EC2?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS automatically manages and applies OS updates for Amazon RDS; the customer must manually manage and apply OS updates for Amazon EC2

options.label: B
options.text: The customer must patch the OS on Amazon RDS; AWS patches the OS on Amazon EC2

options.label: C
options.text: Neither RDS nor EC2 require operating system updates

options.label: D
options.text: Both RDS and EC2 are automatically updated by the Linux foundation

explanation: Because RDS is a managed service, AWS handles OS patching; for EC2 (IaaS), the customer controls and applies OS patches.

questionText: A company requires all data at rest to be encrypted using AES-256. Whose responsibility is it to activate encryption on an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Enterprise Support

options.label: C
options.text: The hardware vendor

options.label: D
options.text: The local ISP

explanation: The customer must configure default bucket encryption or specify encryption keys during object uploads.

questionText: Who is responsible for ensuring that an application complies with industry privacy laws like GDPR or HIPAA when hosted on AWS?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS

options.label: C
options.text: The AWS Trusted Advisor automated bot

options.label: D
options.text: The open source software community

explanation: While AWS provides compliant infrastructure (e.g., signing BAAs), the customer is responsible for ensuring their specific application and data handling comply with legal regulations.

questionText: What does AWS guarantee regarding physical media that is removed from service due to hardware failure or upgrades?

options.label: A
options.text: Media is sanitized, degaussed, or physically destroyed according to NIST SP 800-88 guidelines before leaving AWS physical control

options.label: B
options.text: Defective hard drives are sold to local retail consumers at discount prices

options.label: C
options.text: Drives are returned directly to the customer's headquarters

options.label: D
options.text: Customer data is left intact on recycled equipment

explanation: AWS uses strict destruction procedures (degaussing, shredding, destroying) aligned with NIST 800-88 so customer data can never be recovered from decommissioned drives.

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which customer action prevents unauthorized API calls to AWS resources?

options.label: A
options.text: Securing and rotating IAM access keys and avoiding hard-coding keys into public code repositories

options.label: B
options.text: Installing security cameras outside the customer's home office

options.label: C
options.text: Using non-standard power cords for laptops

options.label: D
options.text: Requesting a physical tour of an AWS data center

explanation: Safeguarding IAM access keys prevents malicious actors from calling AWS APIs and provisioning unauthorized resources.

questionText: If an organization deploys containers on AWS Fargate, what infrastructure task is removed from their responsibility compared to Amazon EC2?

options.label: A
options.text: Managing, configuring, and patching virtual server host operating systems

options.label: B
options.text: Writing container application code

options.label: C
options.text: Configuring container task memory and CPU limits

options.label: D
options.text: Assigning IAM execution roles to tasks

explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers; AWS manages the underlying EC2 instances and OS, eliminating host maintenance for customers.

questionText: Which customer task ensures high availability for an application deployed across Amazon EC2 instances?

options.label: A
options.text: Configuring Auto Scaling and deploying instances across multiple Availability Zones

options.label: B
options.text: Demanding that AWS install duplicate power cables to their local office

options.label: C
options.text: Restarting the instance manually every 24 hours

options.label: D
options.text: Changing the instance IP address daily

explanation: Customers architect high availability by distributing workloads across multiple AZs and configuring load balancing and Auto Scaling.

questionText: Who is responsible for maintaining the hypervisor layer that isolates virtual machines on Amazon EC2 physical hosts?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS

options.label: B
options.text: The customer

options.label: C
options.text: The operating system creator

options.label: D
options.text: The third-party network provider

explanation: The hypervisor is part of the AWS virtualization infrastructure ('Security OF the Cloud'); AWS manages, patches, and secures it.

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for managing cryptographic keys created in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer manages key policies, rotation settings, and usage permissions for customer managed keys (CMKs)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Support engineers manually approve each decryption request

options.label: C
options.text: The local public utility provider

options.label: D
options.text: The internet certificate authority

explanation: Customers create, rotate, and define IAM access policies for Customer Managed Keys in AWS KMS.

questionText: Which of the following describes customer responsibility for network traffic within an Amazon VPC?

options.label: A
options.text: Configuring routing tables, internet gateways, NAT gateways, and subnet access control lists

options.label: B
options.text: Maintaining physical fiber optic patch panels inside AWS routing rooms

options.label: C
options.text: Upgrading physical switch firmware

options.label: D
options.text: Testing undersea telecommunications cables

explanation: Customers design and configure their virtual network topology, including routing rules, gateways, and subnets within their VPC.

questionText: When an application stores credit card numbers in an Amazon S3 bucket, whose responsibility is it to ensure compliance with PCI DSS requirements for cardholder data protection?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer is responsible for protecting cardholder data inside their application and bucket configurations

options.label: B
options.text: AWS takes on all PCI DSS liability for stored customer credit cards

options.label: C
options.text: The credit card issuing bank handles all bucket encryption automatically

options.label: D
options.text: PCI DSS does not apply to cloud environments

explanation: AWS provides a PCI DSS Level 1 compliant physical platform, but the customer must implement data protection, tokenization, and access controls for cardholder data.

questionText: Who is responsible for physical disaster recovery of an AWS facility destroyed by an earthquake?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS

options.label: B
options.text: The customer

options.label: C
options.text: The hardware insurance broker

options.label: D
options.text: The local city council

explanation: AWS manages physical facility resilience, backup power, and rebuilding hardware infrastructure following physical disasters.

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which responsibility belongs to the customer when launching instances from an Amazon Machine Image (AMI)?

options.label: A
options.text: Configuring user credentials, SSH keys, security software, and application firewall rules on the instance

options.label: B
options.text: Constructing the physical hypervisor server chassis

options.label: C
options.text: Providing electricity to the server rack

options.label: D
options.text: Wiring network cables between host computers

explanation: Once an instance is launched from an AMI, securing SSH access, managing user accounts, and hardening the OS is the customer's job.

questionText: What are two security responsibilities of AWS under the Shared Responsibility Model? Select TWO.

options.label: A
options.text: Maintaining environmental controls (HVAC, fire suppression) in data centers

options.label: B
options.text: Patching vulnerabilities in the virtualization hypervisor software

options.label: C
options.text: Configuring customer IAM role policies

options.label: D
options.text: Rotating passwords for customer database administrators

options.label: E
options.text: Setting up S3 bucket public access blocks

explanation: Data center environmental controls and hypervisor software maintenance are foundational responsibilities of AWS.

questionText: Who is responsible for configuring multi-region data replication for an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer (by enabling Cross-Region Replication in bucket settings)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS automatically replicates all S3 buckets to every region worldwide by default

options.label: C
options.text: The local telecommunication carrier

options.label: D
options.text: The web browser manufacturer

explanation: S3 stores data redundantly across multiple AZs in one Region by default; cross-region replication (CRR) is an optional feature configured by the customer.

questionText: Why is customer awareness and security training considered a shared control?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS trains AWS personnel to protect physical infrastructure, while customers must train their employees to follow secure cloud practices

options.label: B
options.text: AWS provides mandatory in-person classroom teaching for all registered AWS users

options.label: C
options.text: Customers must physically train AWS data center guards

options.label: D
options.text: There are no security training requirements in the cloud

explanation: Both entities must educate their own workforce on operational and data security procedures.

questionText: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which action is required of a customer who suspects an unauthorized employee has compromised an IAM access key?

options.label: A
options.text: Deactivate or delete the compromised access key immediately and generate a new key

options.label: B
options.text: Submit a support ticket and wait 3 business days for AWS to investigate

options.label: C
options.text: Shut down all AWS data centers globally

options.label: D
options.text: Post the access key to a public forum to alert other users

explanation: Managing access keys is a customer responsibility; compromised credentials must be invalidated immediately by the customer via IAM.

questionText: What is the recommended best practice for the AWS account root user after initial account setup?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), lock away the root credentials, and create individual IAM users for daily administrative tasks

options.label: B
options.text: Share the root user password with all team developers

options.label: C
options.text: Generate root access keys and commit them to public GitHub repositories

options.label: D
options.text: Use the root user account for routine daily CLI deployments

explanation: AWS strongly recommends enabling MFA on the root user, never creating root access keys, and using least-privilege IAM users/roles for daily tasks.

questionText: Which AWS service is used to manage identities, permissions, and access controls for users and resources at no additional charge?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Inspector

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Shield

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Artifact

explanation: AWS IAM is the core identity governance service in AWS, allowing granular permission management without additional fees.

questionText: What is an IAM Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A formal JSON document that defines allowed or denied permissions to AWS services and resources

options.label: B
options.text: A physical contract signed with AWS sales representatives

options.label: C
options.text: A Python script that launches EC2 instances

options.label: D
options.text: A network routing table for a VPC

explanation: An IAM policy is a JSON document containing statements that define explicit Allow or Deny actions on specific AWS resources.

questionText: Which element in an IAM policy statement specifies whether the statement results in an allow or an explicit deny?

options.label: A
options.text: Effect

options.label: B
options.text: Action

options.label: C
options.text: Resource

options.label: D
options.text: Principal

explanation: The 'Effect' element in an IAM policy statement must be set to either 'Allow' or 'Deny'.

questionText: If an IAM user has two policies attached—one granting 'Allow' for s3:GetObject and another granting 'Deny' for s3:GetObject on the same bucket—what is the user's effective access?

options.label: A
options.text: Access is DENIED (an explicit Deny always overrides an Allow in IAM evaluation)

options.label: B
options.text: Access is ALLOWED because the Allow was attached first

options.label: C
options.text: Access is granted only on alternate Tuesdays

options.label: D
options.text: The user's account is permanently deleted

explanation: In AWS IAM permission evaluation, an explicit Deny always overrides any Allow statements.

questionText: What is an IAM Role?

options.label: A
options.text: An IAM identity that can be assumed by trusted entities (such as EC2 instances or Lambda functions) to obtain temporary security credentials

options.label: B
options.text: A collection of permanent usernames and passwords

options.label: C
options.text: A physical security card used at AWS offices

options.label: D
options.text: A dedicated server with special privileges

explanation: An IAM role is assumed temporarily by identities or services, issuing temporary security credentials via AWS STS rather than permanent access keys.

questionText: Why should an application running on an Amazon EC2 instance use an IAM Role instead of hard-coded access keys?

options.label: A
options.text: IAM roles provide temporary credentials that rotate automatically without embedding sensitive secrets in code

options.label: B
options.text: IAM roles are the only way to run Linux instances

options.label: C
options.text: Hard-coded access keys increase network latency by 400%

options.label: D
options.text: IAM roles make instances completely free of charge

explanation: Attaching an IAM role to an EC2 instance allows the instance to securely retrieve temporary credentials, avoiding the severe risk of hard-coded secrets.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)?

options.label: A
options.text: To add an extra layer of security beyond a username and password by requiring a secondary verification token

options.label: B
options.text: To allow users to log in without entering a password

options.label: C
options.text: To speed up network data transfer rates

options.label: D
options.text: To share a single account among multiple developers

explanation: MFA requires a second authentication factor (such as an authenticator app code or hardware token), protecting accounts against stolen passwords.

questionText: Which types of MFA devices are supported for AWS account login? Select TWO.

options.label: A
options.text: Virtual authenticator applications (such as Google Authenticator or Authy)

options.label: B
options.text: FIDO-certified physical hardware security keys (such as YubiKeys)

options.label: C
options.text: Unencrypted text files emailed to customer support

options.label: D
options.text: Physical copper wire loops

options.label: E
options.text: Standard credit card magnetic stripes

explanation: AWS supports virtual MFA apps (time-based one-time passwords) and FIDO-compliant hardware security keys.

questionText: What is an IAM Group?

options.label: A
options.text: A collection of IAM users used to specify permissions for multiple users at once

options.label: B
options.text: An identity that can be assumed by applications

options.label: C
options.text: A cluster of EC2 instances running identical software

options.label: D
options.text: A shared email inbox managed by AWS

explanation: An IAM group lets administrators assign policies to multiple users simultaneously (e.g., an 'Admins' or 'Developers' group).

questionText: Can an IAM Group be identified as a Principal in an IAM policy statement?

options.label: A
options.text: No, an IAM group cannot be a Principal in a resource-based policy; permissions are attached to the group to affect member users

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, groups can assume roles directly

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, groups can log in to the AWS console with a group password

options.label: D
options.text: Only in the us-east-1 region

explanation: IAM groups are strictly management containers for users; they cannot log in directly or be named as Principals in resource policies.

questionText: What credentials are used to authenticate programmatic requests to AWS through the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs?

options.label: A
options.text: Access Key ID and Secret Access Key

options.label: B
options.text: Username and console password

options.label: C
options.text: Home mailing address and zip code

options.label: D
options.text: Browser cookie session ID

explanation: Programmatic access to AWS APIs via CLI or SDK utilizes Access Key IDs and Secret Access Keys.

questionText: Which AWS IAM tool generates a downloadable CSV report listing all account users and the status of their passwords, access keys, and MFA devices?

options.label: A
options.text: IAM Credential Report

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Inspector

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Cost Explorer

explanation: The IAM Credential Report is an audit document listing all users and their credential ages, rotation histories, and MFA status.

questionText: Which IAM tool helps identify which resources (such as S3 buckets or IAM roles) are shared with an external entity outside the AWS account?

options.label: A
options.text: IAM Access Analyzer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CloudFormation

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Macie

explanation: IAM Access Analyzer evaluates resource-based policies to identify unintended external access to your AWS resources.

questionText: Which design principle recommends granting users only the specific permissions needed to complete their daily job tasks and nothing more?

options.label: A
options.text: Principle of Least Privilege

options.label: B
options.text: Principle of Infinite Redundancy

options.label: C
options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale

options.label: D
options.text: Stop guessing capacity

explanation: The Principle of Least Privilege minimizes risk by ensuring users have only the minimum necessary permissions.

questionText: A new junior developer needs read-only access to Amazon S3. How should the administrator grant this access following best practices?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach the AWS-managed policy 'AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess' to the user or developer group

options.label: B
options.text: Attach the 'AdministratorAccess' policy to the user

options.label: C
options.text: Provide the junior developer with the root user login credentials

options.label: D
options.text: Make all S3 buckets completely public on the internet

explanation: Using pre-built AWS Managed Policies like 'AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess' grants precise least-privilege permissions without administrative sprawl.

questionText: What happens if an action is neither explicitly allowed nor explicitly denied in an IAM policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Access is DENIED by default (implicit deny)

options.label: B
options.text: Access is automatically granted

options.label: C
options.text: The request is delayed by 1 hour

options.label: D
options.text: The user is prompted to pay a microtransaction

explanation: By default, all requests are implicitly denied unless an applicable IAM policy statement explicitly grants Allow.

questionText: Which of the following is an example of an AWS Identity-Based Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A policy attached directly to an IAM user, group, or role

options.label: B
options.text: A policy attached directly to an Amazon S3 bucket

options.label: C
options.text: A key policy attached to an AWS KMS key

options.label: D
options.text: A VPC endpoint policy

explanation: Identity-based policies are JSON permission documents attached directly to IAM users, groups, or roles.

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a Resource-Based Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: An Amazon S3 Bucket Policy

options.label: B
options.text: An IAM Group policy attached to Developers

options.label: C
options.text: An IAM Role execution policy

options.label: D
options.text: An AWS Budgets alert threshold

explanation: Resource-based policies (such as S3 bucket policies, KMS key policies, or SQS queue policies) are attached directly to the resource itself.

questionText: What security risk occurs when developers hard-code permanent AWS access keys into mobile app binaries or public GitHub repos?

options.label: A
options.text: Malicious third parties can extract the keys and make unauthorized API calls to compromise or abuse account resources

options.label: B
options.text: The mobile app will crash because AWS keys only run on supercomputers

options.label: C
options.text: AWS will confiscate the mobile phone hardware

options.label: D
options.text: The app will be converted to a desktop application automatically

explanation: Exposing permanent credentials publicly allows attackers to launch unauthorized compute, mine cryptocurrency, or steal confidential data.

questionText: How often does AWS recommend rotating IAM access keys as a security best practice?

options.label: A
options.text: Regularly (e.g. every 90 days)

options.label: B
options.text: Never, access keys should remain permanent forever

options.label: C
options.text: Every 5 seconds

options.label: D
options.text: Only once every 20 years

explanation: Regular credential rotation limits the duration that compromised keys can be exploited.

questionText: Which AWS service issues temporary, limited-privilege security credentials for IAM roles?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Artifact

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Pricing Calculator

explanation: AWS STS generates short-lived credentials (session tokens) for IAM roles and federated users.

questionText: What is federated identity management in AWS IAM?

options.label: A
options.text: Allowing users from an external corporate identity provider (such as Microsoft Active Directory or Okta) to access AWS using single sign-on (SSO)

options.label: B
options.text: Creating duplicate root user accounts for every employee

options.label: C
options.text: Connecting five physical monitors to one computer

options.label: D
options.text: Running AWS services exclusively on federal government servers

explanation: Identity federation allows enterprise users to sign in to AWS using their existing corporate credentials without creating individual IAM users.

questionText: What is the function of the 'Condition' block in an IAM policy statement?

options.label: A
options.text: To specify contextual requirements (such as client IP address range, MFA status, or date) that must be met for the policy to take effect

options.label: B
options.text: To translate the policy text into multiple languages

options.label: C
options.text: To calculate the financial cost of running the action

options.label: D
options.text: To specify which brand of computer the developer uses

explanation: The Condition block specifies circumstances (like aws:SourceIP or aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent) under which policy statements apply.

questionText: Which account credential should NEVER be shared among multiple human administrators under any circumstances?

options.label: A
options.text: The AWS account root user credentials

options.label: B
options.text: The company website public URL

options.label: C
options.text: The AWS pricing documentation link

options.label: D
options.text: The public S3 bucket website endpoint

explanation: The root user has unrestricted superuser access to all resources and billing; sharing root credentials creates severe security and auditing risks.

questionText: What is an AWS Managed Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A standalone policy created, versioned, and maintained by AWS that aligns with common job functions

options.label: B
options.text: A policy written by third-party freelancers

options.label: C
options.text: A policy that can only be used on-premises

options.label: D
options.text: A policy that charges $5 per API call

explanation: AWS Managed Policies are authored and updated by AWS for common roles (e.g. AdministratorAccess, ReadOnlyAccess).

questionText: What is a Customer Managed Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A standalone IAM policy created and customized by the customer to meet specific organizational requirements

options.label: B
options.text: A policy created automatically by Amazon S3

options.label: C
options.text: A policy written exclusively in C++ code

options.label: D
options.text: A physical document mailed to AWS headquarters

explanation: Customer Managed Policies give full control over custom permissions tailored to an organization's specific resource ARNs and actions.

questionText: What is an Inline Policy in IAM?

options.label: A
options.text: A policy embedded directly and exclusively into a single specific IAM user, group, or role

options.label: B
options.text: A policy that is broadcast to the public internet

options.label: C

explanation: AWS Firewall Manager centrally configures and manages firewall rules across accounts and resources in AWS Organizations.

questionText: What security advantage does an Amazon VPC Private Subnet provide for backend database instances?

options.label: A
options.text: Instances in a private subnet do not possess public IP addresses and cannot be reached directly from the public internet

options.label: B
options.text: Instances in private subnets cannot run database software

options.label: C
options.text: Private subnets make data queries 1000 times faster

options.label: D
options.text: Private subnets are physically located on Mars

explanation: Private subnets have no direct route to an Internet Gateway, shielding critical databases from direct internet exposure.

questionText: What is the purpose of an Amazon VPC NAT Gateway in securing private subnet instances?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows private instances outbound internet access (e.g. for OS security updates) while blocking unauthorized inbound connections from the internet

options.label: B
options.text: It provides public IP addresses to all database servers

options.label: C
options.text: It replaces the need for a database password

options.label: D
options.text: It encrypts physical hard drives

explanation: A NAT Gateway enables outbound internet requests from private subnets (for patches and software) while preventing external internet hosts from initiating inbound sessions.

questionText: Which tool provides automated remediation actions (such as disabling an exposed IAM access key) when an alert is triggered in AWS Security Hub?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Security Hub custom actions routed through Amazon EventBridge to AWS Lambda functions

options.label: B
options.text: A phone call to the local police

options.label: C
options.text: An S3 lifecycle rule

options.label: D
options.text: A manual printout of the alert

explanation: Security Hub integrates with EventBridge and Lambda to execute automated custom remediation workflows in real-time.

questionText: How does Amazon Inspector scan container images for vulnerabilities?

options.label: A
options.text: It automatically scans images pushed to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) for known software package flaws

options.label: B
options.text: It unzips container images onto local laptops

options.label: C
options.text: It requires developers to rewrite containers in HTML

options.label: D
options.text: It requires shipping USB flash drives to AWS

explanation: Amazon Inspector natively integrates with Amazon ECR, scanning container images automatically on push or continuously over time.

questionText: Which AWS service tracks resource configuration changes over time and assesses whether those configurations comply with internal security rules?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Config

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Snowball

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Budgets

explanation: AWS Config continuously monitors and records resource configurations, evaluating them against desired compliance rules (e.g. 's3-bucket-ssl-requests-only').

questionText: What happens when an AWS Config managed rule discovers a non-compliant resource (e.g. an unencrypted EBS volume)?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Config flags the resource as 'NON_COMPLIANT' on the dashboard and can trigger automated remediation via Systems Manager Automation

options.label: B
options.text: AWS automatically terminates the customer account

options.label: C
options.text: The data volume is deleted instantly without warning

options.label: D
options.text: All employees receive a penalty deduction from their paycheck

explanation: AWS Config marks non-compliant resources and can initiate automatic remediation actions (e.g. applying encryption or snapshotting).

questionText: What is the primary benefit of using AWS Secrets Manager rather than AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for database passwords?

options.label: A
options.text: Secrets Manager provides native automated credential rotation capabilities with built-in Lambda templates for databases

options.label: B
options.text: Parameter Store is completely unencrypted

options.label: C
options.text: Secrets Manager is only available for government agencies

options.label: D
options.text: Parameter Store cannot store string values

explanation: Secrets Manager natively automates scheduled password rotation for databases, while Parameter Store is primarily for configuration management.

questionText: Which service can automatically protect web applications against HTTP flood (layer 7) DDoS attacks using rate-based rules?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS WAF

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Artifact

explanation: Rate-based rules in AWS WAF track request rates from individual client IPs and block IPs that exceed defined thresholds (e.g., >2,000 requests per 5 minutes).

questionText: What is the function of AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policies?

options.label: A
options.text: To serve as the primary resource-based access control document determining who can manage and use the KMS key

options.label: B
options.text: To set the physical price of server racks

options.label: C
options.text: To measure network packet delay

options.label: D
options.text: To configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups

explanation: KMS key policies are mandatory resource-based policies attached to every KMS key; without permission in the key policy, no entity can use the key.

questionText: Which AWS service provides an audit log of who made which API call, from which IP address, and at what time?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS CloudTrail

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Metrics

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Pricing Calculator

explanation: AWS CloudTrail captures all management and data API calls made via Console, CLI, or SDKs, recording identity, timestamp, and source IP.

questionText: How does Amazon GuardDuty protect AWS accounts against compromised IAM credentials used from foreign countries?

options.label: A
options.text: It flags anomalous API calls made from unusual geographic locations or IP addresses associated with known bad actors

options.label: B
options.text: It cancels the user's passport

options.label: C
options.text: It converts the user's currency to Bitcoin

options.label: D
options.text: It blocks all foreign internet traffic to the entire country

explanation: GuardDuty applies machine learning to CloudTrail events, alerting on anomalous access locations, unusual API calls, and leaked credentials.

questionText: What is the recommended encryption practice for data stored in Amazon S3 buckets containing confidential business records?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Server-Side Encryption (SSE-KMS or SSE-S3) so all stored objects are automatically encrypted at rest

options.label: B
options.text: Leave objects unencrypted because S3 is private by default

options.label: C
options.text: Store data on unencrypted text files

options.label: D
options.text: Email the files to developers before uploading

explanation: Server-Side Encryption protects data at rest automatically on Amazon S3 storage media using AES-256 encryption.

questionText: Which AWS service allows creating private dedicated network connections between an on-premises data center and AWS that bypass the public internet entirely, improving security?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Shield

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated private fiber links from on-premises facilities to AWS, bypassing public internet security risks.

questionText: What is an AWS Region?

options.label: A
options.text: A single physical data center located in a major metropolitan city

options.label: B
options.text: A physical geographical location in the world with multiple isolated Availability Zones connected by low-latency networks

options.label: C
options.text: A virtual private network endpoint used exclusively for edge content caching

options.label: D
options.text: A collection of edge servers distributed within a single country

explanation: An AWS Region is a physical geographical location around the world where AWS clusters data centers. Each Region consists of multiple (at least 3 in modern regions), isolated, and physically separated Availability Zones connected via low-latency, redundant fiber networks.

questionText: Which statement best describes an AWS Availability Zone (AZ)?

options.label: A
options.text: A collection of edge locations within a continent used to deliver DNS records

options.label: B
options.text: One or more discrete physical data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region

options.label: C
options.text: A logical grouping of AWS accounts for consolidated organization billing

options.label: D
options.text: A geographic boundary defining national data sovereignty compliance

explanation: An Availability Zone (AZ) consists of one or more discrete physical data centers, each with independent, redundant power, cooling, and physical security, housed in separate facilities within an AWS Region.

questionText: A company requires single-digit millisecond latency for mobile edge computing applications connected via 5G networks. Which AWS service or deployment model is designed for this?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Wavelength

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowcone

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Route 53

explanation: AWS Wavelength brings AWS compute and storage services to the edge of telecommunications carriers' 5G networks, enabling developers to build applications that deliver ultra-low latency to mobile devices and end users.

questionText: Which AWS infrastructure offering allows customers to run AWS compute, storage, and database services natively on-premises in their own corporate data centers?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Local Zones

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Outposts

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

explanation: AWS Outposts brings native AWS services, infrastructure, and operating models to virtually any data center, co-location space, or on-premises facility for a truly consistent hybrid experience.

questionText: What is an AWS Local Zone?

options.label: A
options.text: A specialized AWS Region located exclusively outside North America

options.label: B
options.text: An extension of an AWS Region that places compute, storage, and database services closer to large populations and industry centers

options.label: C
options.text: A local software cache deployed on an on-premises physical server

options.label: D
options.text: An isolated corporate subnet configured without an Internet Gateway

explanation: AWS Local Zones place compute, storage, database, and other select AWS services closer to end-users in large population, industry, and IT centers where no AWS Region currently exists, achieving single-digit millisecond latency.

questionText: Which factors should guide the selection of an AWS Region for deploying workloads? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Proximity to end users to minimize network latency

options.label: B
options.text: Legal and regulatory compliance requirements regarding data residency

options.label: C
options.text: Ensuring that the root account password never expires

options.label: D
options.text: Guaranteeing that EC2 Spot instances will never be interrupted

options.label: E
options.text: The exact number of IAM users registered in the account

explanation: Key factors when choosing an AWS Region include: 1) Proximity to end users (reducing latency), 2) Compliance and data residency laws (legal requirements), 3) Service availability (some services roll out in specific regions first), and 4) Cost variation across regions.

questionText: What component of AWS Global Infrastructure delivers content with lower latency by caching copies of data closer to global users?

options.label: A
options.text: Edge Locations (Point of Presence)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Transit Gateways

options.label: C
options.text: Virtual Private Gateways

options.label: D
options.text: Customer Gateways

explanation: Edge Locations (Points of Presence) are global data centers maintained by AWS and utilized by services like Amazon CloudFront and Route 53 to cache and distribute content closer to end-users worldwide with minimal latency.

questionText: How are Availability Zones within the same AWS Region interconnected?

options.label: A
options.text: Via the public Internet through IPSec VPN tunnels

options.label: B
options.text: Via high-speed, high-bandwidth, fully redundant, low-latency dedicated optical networking

options.label: C
options.text: Via satellite links with 1-second transit delays

options.label: D
options.text: Through on-premises customer switching hubs

explanation: All Availability Zones in an AWS Region are interconnected with high-bandwidth, low-latency networking over fully redundant, dedicated metro-fiber loops, enabling synchronous replication and fault-tolerant architectures.

questionText: Which AWS services operate globally without requiring you to select a specific geographic Region in the AWS Management Console? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon EC2

options.label: B
options.text: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management)

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon EBS

options.label: E
options.text: Amazon RDS

explanation: AWS IAM, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon Route 53, and AWS WAF (global) are global services whose administrative consoles and core endpoints do not require regional scoping, whereas EC2, EBS, and RDS are strictly regional.

questionText: What is the primary advantage of deploying an application across multiple Availability Zones in a single Region?

options.label: A
options.text: Eliminating all data transfer costs completely

options.label: B
options.text: High availability and fault tolerance against localized physical data center failures

options.label: C
options.text: Automatic zero-downtime database schema migrations

options.label: D
options.text: Decreasing software licensing fees by 50%

explanation: Deploying across multiple AZs ensures that if a localized issue (power outage, flooding, hardware failure) strikes one data center/AZ, workloads seamlessly continue running in the remaining operational AZs without catastrophic outage.

questionText: What is the minimum number of Availability Zones present in any standard modern AWS Region?
explanation: Every standard modern AWS Region consists of a minimum of three isolated and physically separated Availability Zones (some historical older regions launched with two, but the standard architecture requires at least three).

questionText: Which statement regarding data replication between AWS Regions is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS automatically replicates all customer data across every global region by default

options.label: B
options.text: No customer data is replicated outside a chosen Region unless explicitly configured by the customer

options.label: C
options.text: AWS stores encrypted backups in an undisclosed global region without user consent

options.label: D
options.text: Replication between regions is forbidden by AWS security policy

explanation: AWS will never replicate or move customer data outside of the customer's explicitly chosen Region without the customer's explicit command or configuration (e.g., S3 Cross-Region Replication). Customer data residency is strictly respected.

questionText: What is a Regional Edge Cache in Amazon CloudFront?

options.label: A
options.text: An on-premises storage appliance shipped to branch offices

options.label: B
options.text: A caching tier located between CloudFront Edge Locations and the origin server for less-frequently accessed content

options.label: C
options.text: A local tape drive library for archival compliance

options.label: D
options.text: A cold storage Glacier vault embedded within an EC2 subnet

explanation: Regional Edge Caches are CloudFront points located between your origin server and Edge Locations. They have larger cache capacities to retain content longer, preventing edge locations from needing to query the origin server as often.

questionText: Which AWS infrastructure resource is physically closest to the end user for accelerating DNS queries and static web assets?

options.label: A
options.text: Availability Zone

options.label: B
options.text: Edge Location

options.label: C
options.text: Outpost

options.label: D
options.text: Primary Region

explanation: Edge Locations are distributed across hundreds of major population centers worldwide to bring DNS resolution (Route 53) and cached content (CloudFront) as physically close to end users as possible.

questionText: What technology enables AWS Regions to be isolated while sharing a private global backbone?

options.label: A
options.text: The AWS global network backbone, constructed with private fiber links independent of the public Internet

options.label: B
options.text: Public Tor relays

options.label: C
options.text: Commercial satellite broadcast networks

options.label: D
options.text: Municipal copper telephone wiring

explanation: AWS owns and operates a purpose-built, highly available, redundant private fiber global network backbone that carries inter-region and edge-to-region traffic without traversing the public Internet.

questionText: When designing a disaster recovery architecture with an RPO of hours, which deployment model provides geographical separation across thousands of miles?

options.label: A
options.text: Multi-AZ within us-east-1

options.label: B
options.text: Multi-Region (e.g., us-east-1 and us-west-2)

options.label: C
options.text: Single AZ with RAID-1 EBS volumes

options.label: D
options.text: Single instance store with local snapshots

explanation: Multi-Region deployments provide geographic resilience against regional disasters (such as massive natural disasters or geopolitical events affecting an entire state or country).

questionText: Why does AWS assign letters (e.g., us-east-1a, us-east-1b) independently across different customer accounts?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent all customers from launching resources into the exact same physical data center and exhausting physical capacity

options.label: B
options.text: Because the letters represent different pricing tiers

options.label: C
options.text: To enforce different levels of IAM encryption per account

options.label: D
options.text: To restrict certain accounts from using high-performance instances

explanation: To distribute resources evenly across the physical data centers in a Region, AWS independently maps AZ letter identifiers (us-east-1a) to physical AZ IDs (e.g., use1-az1) for each customer account.

questionText: If an enterprise needs to comply with strict national data residency laws requiring healthcare records to remain inside Germany, what should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploy workloads solely in the Europe (Frankfurt) AWS Region (eu-central-1)

options.label: B
options.text: Encrypt data in us-east-1 and save keys in a German bank

options.label: C
options.text: Use any Region because AWS automatically routes data based on the passport of the account owner

options.label: D
options.text: Deploy only in AWS GovCloud (US)

explanation: Choosing the specific AWS Region located in the required jurisdiction (e.g., eu-central-1 in Frankfurt, Germany) ensures data remains physically resident in that country to satisfy regulatory and legal requirements.

questionText: What capability allows an administrator to identify the true physical data center mapping across multiple AWS accounts in an organization?

options.label: A
options.text: AZ ID (e.g., use1-az1)
