options.label: B
options.text: VPC Subnet CIDR

options.label: C
options.text: AMI ID

options.label: D
options.text: IAM Role ARN

explanation: AZ IDs (e.g., use1-az1) are consistent physical identifiers across all accounts, allowing administrators to coordinate shared resources and balance workloads across identical physical infrastructure across accounts.

questionText: Which statement is TRUE regarding fault isolation between AWS Regions?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Regions are completely autonomous and isolated from each other to prevent cascade failures

options.label: B
options.text: An outage in one Region will immediately shut down all compute resources in adjacent Regions

options.label: C
options.text: Regions share the same physical power grid and local telecommunications providers

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Regions cannot communicate with each other under any circumstances

explanation: AWS Regions are intentionally engineered to be autonomous and completely isolated from other Regions to maximize fault tolerance and ensure localized failures cannot cascade globally.

questionText: What is the primary function of AWS Points of Presence (PoPs)?

options.label: A
options.text: Hosting primary relational database write replicas

options.label: B
options.text: Delivering cached data and accelerating traffic to applications via CloudFront and Route 53

options.label: C
options.text: Replacing on-premises SAN arrays

options.label: D
options.text: Providing physical desks for AWS engineers

explanation: Points of Presence (PoPs) consist of Edge Locations and Regional Edge Caches designed to cache content, terminate TLS connections closer to clients, and speed up global delivery.

questionText: An online gaming company wants to reduce latency for real-time mobile gameplay in major cities. Which AWS service embeds compute within mobile telco 5G networks?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Wavelength

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Glue

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Step Functions

explanation: AWS Wavelength provides compute and storage within 5G telecommunication networks, offering single-digit millisecond latency for mobile edge applications like interactive streaming and cloud gaming.

questionText: Which statement is true regarding AWS Global Infrastructure availability zones?

options.label: A
options.text: An AZ is always a single server rack in a shared colocation facility

options.label: B
options.text: AZs in a Region are located within meaningful geographic distance to protect against localized disasters, while maintaining low-latency connectivity

options.label: C
options.text: All AZs globally are situated within 5 miles of Seattle, Washington

options.label: D
options.text: An AZ cannot contain more than 10 virtual machines simultaneously

explanation: AZs are separated by meaningful physical distance (often miles apart) to prevent concurrent disruptions from local floods, fires, or power failures, yet close enough for low-latency (<2 ms) synchronous replication.

questionText: Which AWS service utilizes AWS Edge Locations to protect web applications against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Shield

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Cloud9

options.label: C
options.text: AWS DataSync

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Inspector

explanation: AWS Shield and AWS WAF inspect and mitigate DDoS attacks globally at edge locations before malicious traffic ever reaches your backend servers or applications in your VPC.

questionText: What is Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)?

options.label: A
options.text: A web service that provides secure, resizable compute capacity (virtual servers) in the cloud

options.label: B
options.text: A managed relational database engine supporting MySQL and PostgreSQL

options.label: C
options.text: A serverless object storage solution for hosting audio files

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware firewall appliance shipped to corporate branch offices

explanation: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) provides scalable computing capacity in the AWS Cloud, allowing users to launch virtual servers (instances), manage networking and storage, and scale up or down dynamically.

questionText: Which EC2 instance type family is best suited for workloads requiring high memory capacity such as in-memory databases and large enterprise caches?

options.label: A
options.text: Compute Optimized (C family)

options.label: B
options.text: Memory Optimized (R and X families)

options.label: C
options.text: Storage Optimized (I and D families)

options.label: D
options.text: Accelerated Computing (P and G families)

explanation: Memory Optimized instances (such as R6g, R5, X2gd) are engineered to deliver fast performance for workloads that process large data sets in memory, such as Redis caches and in-memory databases.

questionText: Which EC2 instance family is designed for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, media transcoding, and high-performance web servers?

options.label: A
options.text: Compute Optimized (C family)

options.label: B
options.text: General Purpose (M and T families)

options.label: C
options.text: Storage Optimized (H and I families)

options.label: D
options.text: Memory Optimized (R family)

explanation: Compute Optimized instances (C family, e.g., C6g, C5) feature high-performance processors and provide cost-effective compute performance for compute-bound applications.

questionText: Which EC2 instance family uses hardware accelerators or GPUs to perform graphics rendering, machine learning inference, and financial modeling?

options.label: A
options.text: Accelerated Computing (P and G families)

options.label: B
options.text: General Purpose (T4g family)

options.label: C
options.text: Compute Optimized (C6i family)

options.label: D
options.text: Storage Optimized (Im4gn family)

explanation: Accelerated Computing instances (e.g., P4, G5) utilize graphics processing units (GPUs) or dedicated hardware accelerators to accelerate machine learning, scientific computing, and graphic-intensive tasks.

questionText: Which EC2 purchasing option provides the greatest cost discount (up to 90%) in exchange for instances that can be reclaimed by AWS with a 2-minute warning?

options.label: A
options.text: On-Demand Instances

options.label: B
options.text: Spot Instances

options.label: C
options.text: Reserved Instances

options.label: D
options.text: Dedicated Hosts

explanation: EC2 Spot Instances let you take advantage of unused EC2 capacity in the AWS cloud at steep discounts (up to 90% compared to On-Demand prices), but they can be interrupted when AWS needs the capacity back.

questionText: A company has unpredictable, short-term workloads that cannot be interrupted and must run without upfront commitments or long-term contracts. Which pricing option is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Spot Instances

options.label: B
options.text: On-Demand Instances

options.label: C
options.text: 3-Year Standard Reserved Instances

options.label: D
options.text: EC2 Savings Plans

explanation: On-Demand Instances let you pay for compute capacity by the second or hour without long-term commitments or upfront fees, making them ideal for short-term, irregular, or unpredictable workloads that cannot be interrupted.

questionText: A company has a steady-state web backend running continuously 24/7 with predictable baseline compute usage for the next 3 years. Which options provide cost savings? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: EC2 Savings Plans

options.label: B
options.text: Reserved Instances (RIs)

options.label: C
options.text: Spot Instances

options.label: D
options.text: On-Demand Instances

options.label: E
options.text: Dedicated Hosts without commitment

explanation: Both Savings Plans and Reserved Instances (1-year or 3-year commitments) offer significant discounts (up to 72%) for steady-state, predictable baseline workloads in exchange for committing to a consistent usage amount.

questionText: What is a major advantage of EC2 Compute Savings Plans over Standard Reserved Instances?

options.label: A
options.text: Savings Plans apply automatically across instance families, operating systems, regions, and even to AWS Fargate and Lambda

options.label: B
options.text: Savings Plans are completely free of charge and require zero payment commitment

options.label: C
options.text: Savings Plans guarantee that hardware components will never fail

options.label: D
options.text: Savings Plans allow unlimited instances to be launched without service limits

explanation: Compute Savings Plans provide high flexibility: they offer up to 66% discount and automatically apply to EC2 instance usage regardless of instance family, size, OS, tenancy, or Region, as well as AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda.

questionText: An enterprise has strict regulatory licensing terms that require software to run on physical, dedicated server hardware where socket and core counts are visible. Which option satisfies this?

options.label: A
options.text: EC2 Dedicated Hosts

options.label: B
options.text: EC2 Spot Instances

options.label: C
options.text: Multi-Tenant On-Demand Instances

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon LightSail

explanation: EC2 Dedicated Hosts provide a physical server dedicated entirely to your use, giving visibility and control over instance placement at the host level, which helps satisfy Bring-Your-Own-License (BYOL) compliance requirements.

questionText: What is the difference between EC2 Dedicated Instances and EC2 Dedicated Hosts?

options.label: A
options.text: Dedicated Hosts provide physical server visibility (sockets/cores) and host-level licensing control; Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware without host control

options.label: B
options.text: Dedicated Instances are free while Dedicated Hosts are paid

options.label: C
options.text: Dedicated Instances are only deployed in local zones

options.label: D
options.text: There is no difference between them

explanation: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single customer account at the instance level. Dedicated Hosts also provide dedicated hardware but add physical server visibility, host socket/core control, and BYOL license support.

questionText: What is an Amazon Machine Image (AMI)?

options.label: A
options.text: A template that contains the software configuration (operating system, application server, and applications) required to launch an EC2 instance

options.label: B
options.text: A photo album service for storing high-resolution JPEG files

options.label: C
options.text: A real-time screenshot capture tool for auditing server desktops

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware accelerator card plugged into an on-premises workstation

explanation: An AMI is a master image template providing the information required to launch an EC2 instance, including the operating system, pre-installed software packages, configurations, and storage volume mappings.

questionText: Which sources can you use to obtain an Amazon Machine Image (AMI)? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Marketplace (commercial and open-source AMIs packaged by third parties)

options.label: B
options.text: Custom AMIs created from existing configured EC2 instances

options.label: C
options.text: Direct download links from unverified public peer-to-peer torrents

options.label: D
options.text: Importing physical hard drives via postal courier without validation

options.label: E
options.text: Extracting images from AWS IAM policies

explanation: AMIs can be AWS-provided (quickstart), customized by creating an image from your own configured EC2 instance, purchased/subscribed to via the AWS Marketplace, or shared by other AWS accounts.

questionText: What happens when an Amazon EC2 instance backed by an EBS root volume is stopped?

options.label: A
options.text: The instance shuts down, compute charges stop, and data on the EBS root volume persists

options.label: B
options.text: The instance and all attached EBS volumes are permanently deleted

options.label: C
options.text: The instance continues incurring full compute hourly rates

options.label: D
options.text: The instance is automatically migrated to another AWS Region

explanation: When an EBS-backed instance is stopped, compute (CPU/RAM) billing ceases immediately. Data on the attached EBS root volume remains intact, and standard EBS volume storage fees continue to apply.

questionText: What happens to data stored on an EC2 Instance Store volume when the EC2 instance is stopped or terminated?

options.label: A
options.text: The data is permanently lost because instance store is ephemeral temporary storage

options.label: B
options.text: The data is automatically archived to S3 Glacier Deep Archive

options.label: C
options.text: The data is moved to an EBS volume without charge

options.label: D
options.text: The data remains accessible upon restart

explanation: Instance Store volumes provide temporary, ephemeral block storage directly attached to the host server. When the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated, all data on the instance store volume is permanently lost.

questionText: Which feature allows an EC2 instance to preserve its in-memory (RAM) state across stopping and starting, speeding up application boot time?

options.label: A
options.text: EC2 Hibernation

options.label: B
options.text: EC2 Reboot

options.label: C
options.text: Auto Scaling cooldown

options.label: D
options.text: Elastic IP reassignment

explanation: EC2 Hibernation saves the contents from the instance memory (RAM) to your Amazon EBS root volume before stopping. Upon starting, the RAM contents are reloaded, allowing the instance to resume where it left off.

questionText: Which EC2 pricing model is the most economical for fault-tolerant background data processing tasks that can be stopped and resumed at any time?

options.label: A
options.text: Spot Instances

options.label: B
options.text: Dedicated Hosts

options.label: C
options.text: On-Demand Instances

options.label: D
options.text: Multi-Region Reserved Instances

explanation: Spot Instances provide up to 90% savings over On-Demand rates, making them the most cost-effective option for stateless, flexible, or interruptible workloads like big data batch jobs and containerized rendering.

questionText: What is the purpose of EC2 User Data?

options.label: A
options.text: To execute bootstrap configuration scripts automatically during the initial launch of the instance

options.label: B
options.text: To store customer billing credit card information securely

options.label: C
options.text: To record the username and password of the system administrator

options.label: D
options.text: To track user web browsing history across sessions

explanation: EC2 User Data allows you to pass shell scripts or cloud-init directives to an EC2 instance at launch time to automate configuration tasks, package installations, and updates during boot.

questionText: Which AWS service is designed for users who want to deploy a simple website or application with a bundled monthly pricing plan that includes compute, storage, and networking?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Lightsail

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Outposts

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon EKS

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Step Functions

explanation: Amazon Lightsail is an easy-to-use cloud platform that provides virtual private servers, storage, databases, and networking at a low, predictable monthly price, ideal for simple websites and beginner projects.

questionText: What is an Elastic IP address in Amazon EC2?

options.label: A
options.text: A static, public IPv4 address allocated to your account that can be rapidly remapped between instances in the same Region

options.label: B
options.text: A dynamic private IP address assigned by your home ISP

options.label: C
options.text: A free domain name registered through Route 53

options.label: D
options.text: An IPv6 address reserved exclusively for database clusters

explanation: An Elastic IP address is a reserved static public IPv4 address designed for dynamic cloud computing. You can mask instance failures by rapidly remapping the address to another replacement instance in your VPC.

questionText: When an EC2 instance with a default public IP is stopped and started again, what happens to its public IPv4 address?

options.label: A
options.text: The old public IP is released, and a new public IP is assigned from the AWS pool

options.label: B
options.text: The instance retains the exact same public IP permanently without charge

options.label: C
options.text: The instance is automatically converted into an Elastic IP

options.label: D
options.text: Public IP addresses cannot be changed once assigned

explanation: By default, an auto-assigned public IPv4 address is released when an EC2 instance is stopped or terminated. A new public IP is assigned when the instance starts again. To keep a persistent IP, an Elastic IP must be used.

questionText: Which tool provides visual recommendations for selecting the optimal EC2 instance types and sizes based on historical machine learning utilization data?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Compute Optimizer

options.label: B
options.text: AWS X-Ray

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Secrets Manager

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Shield

explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze historical resource utilization metrics (from CloudWatch) and recommends optimal AWS resources (EC2 instance types, EBS volumes, Lambda memory) to reduce costs and improve performance.

questionText: How does AWS calculate billing for EC2 instances running Linux distributions?

options.label: A
options.text: Per-second billing with a 60-second minimum

options.label: B
options.text: Per-day billing rounded up to the nearest week

options.label: C
options.text: Flat annual fee regardless of usage

options.label: D
options.text: Per-megabyte of RAM consumed per hour

explanation: AWS provides per-second billing for EC2 instances launched with open-source Linux distributions (such as Amazon Linux and Ubuntu), with a 60-second minimum duration.

questionText: Which of the following is an example of horizontal scaling for Amazon EC2?

options.label: A
options.text: Adding more EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer to handle increased web traffic

options.label: B
options.text: Changing an EC2 instance type from t3.micro to m5.2xlarge

options.label: C
options.text: Upgrading an EBS volume from 100 GB to 1 TB

options.label: D
options.text: Attaching a secondary network interface card to a single server

explanation: Horizontal scaling (scaling out) involves adding more compute instances to distribute the load across multiple servers. Changing the instance type to a larger size is vertical scaling (scaling up).

questionText: What is vertical scaling in the context of Amazon EC2 compute?

options.label: A
options.text: Upgrading or downgrading the instance size or family (e.g., from t3.small to c5.xlarge) to allocate more CPU and RAM to a single machine

options.label: B
options.text: Deploying replicas across three different continents

options.label: C
options.text: Splitting an application into microservices

options.label: D
options.text: Adding 10 additional servers to an Auto Scaling group

explanation: Vertical scaling (scaling up/down) means resizing a single instance by changing its instance type to one with more or fewer CPUs, memory, network capacity, or storage.

questionText: Which EC2 instance purchase option allows you to exchange attributes (such as instance family, operating system, or tenancy) during the term?

options.label: A
options.text: Convertible Reserved Instances

options.label: B
options.text: Standard Reserved Instances

options.label: C
options.text: Spot Fleet Instances

options.label: D
options.text: On-Demand Instances

explanation: Convertible Reserved Instances allow you to exchange the RI for another Convertible RI with a different instance family, OS, tenancy, or payment option, offering flexibility as architecture requirements change.

questionText: What is the primary benefit of AWS Graviton processors used in modern EC2 instance families (e.g., c7g, m7g, t4g)?

options.label: A
options.text: Superior price-performance engineered on 64-bit ARM architecture compared to traditional x86 processors

options.label: B
options.text: Ability to run legacy 16-bit MS-DOS binaries natively

options.label: C
options.text: Completely eliminating the need for an operating system

options.label: D
options.text: Guaranteeing zero latency regardless of user distance

explanation: AWS Graviton processors are custom-built by AWS using 64-bit ARM Neoverse cores to deliver up to 40% better price-performance over comparable x86-based instances for a wide variety of cloud workloads.

questionText: Which EC2 feature allows you to automatically recover an instance to a healthy physical host if the underlying physical hardware degrades?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon EC2 Instance Auto-Recovery

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Inspector remediation

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Artifact audit

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection

explanation: EC2 Auto-Recovery automatically recovers supported instances if an underlying hardware failure occurs, preserving the instance ID, private and public IP addresses, Elastic IPs, and EBS volume attachments.

questionText: A development team wants to launch a batch job every night at 2 AM that takes 45 minutes to execute. If it fails or is cancelled, it can be safely re-run without issue. Which pricing model is most cost-effective?

options.label: A
options.text: Spot Instances

options.label: B
options.text: Dedicated Host with 3-year upfront payment

options.label: C
options.text: Standard Reserved Instance

options.label: D
options.text: Multi-AZ On-Demand cluster

explanation: Because the workload is stateless, restartable, and runs during off-peak hours, Spot Instances will save up to 90% in compute costs compared to On-Demand.

questionText: Which statement is true regarding the termination protection setting on an EC2 instance?

options.label: A
options.text: It prevents accidental termination of the instance via the AWS Management Console, CLI, or API

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents the operating system from crashing due to software errors

options.label: C
options.text: It disables all SSH access permanently

options.label: D
options.text: It stops AWS from shutting down the instance during billing disputes

explanation: Enabling termination protection on an EC2 instance prevents it from being accidentally terminated by an administrator using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or API calls until the protection is explicitly disabled.

questionText: What key pair component is stored by AWS when you create an EC2 key pair for SSH authentication?

options.label: A
options.text: The public key only; the user downloads and retains the private key

options.label: B
options.text: Both the public key and private key in plain text

options.label: C
options.text: The private key only; the user keeps the public key

options.label: D
options.text: AWS does not store either key component

explanation: AWS stores only the public key component of an EC2 key pair and injects it into the instance metadata at launch. The user must securely download and store the private key file (.pem or .ppk) on their local machine.

questionText: What is AWS Lambda?

options.label: A
options.text: A serverless, event-driven compute service that lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers

options.label: B
options.text: A managed physical blade server rack installed in your office

options.label: C
options.text: A relational database storage engine

options.label: D
options.text: A domain name registrar service

explanation: AWS Lambda lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers. You pay only for the compute time consumed (down to the millisecond) when your code executes in response to events.

questionText: What is the maximum execution execution timeout for a single AWS Lambda function invocation?

options.label: A
options.text: 15 minutes (900 seconds)

options.label: B
options.text: 60 seconds

options.label: C
options.text: 2 hours

options.label: D
options.text: 24 hours

explanation: The maximum configurable execution duration (timeout) for an AWS Lambda function invocation is 15 minutes (900 seconds). For tasks exceeding 15 minutes, AWS Step Functions, ECS, or EC2 should be used.

questionText: How does AWS calculate charges for AWS Lambda executions?

options.label: A
options.text: Based on the number of requests and the duration calculated in milliseconds, multiplied by the allocated memory size

options.label: B
options.text: A flat monthly subscription fee of $50 per function

options.label: C
options.text: Based on the number of lines of source code in the function

options.label: D
options.text: Based on the number of developers with access to the AWS account

explanation: AWS Lambda pricing is determined by: 1) The number of requests/invocations, and 2) The duration of execution measured in milliseconds, weighted by the amount of memory (MB) allocated to the function.

questionText: Which AWS service is a managed container orchestration service compatible with Docker containers?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon DynamoDB

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

explanation: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) is a fully managed container orchestration service that helps you easily deploy, manage, and scale containerized applications using Docker containers.

questionText: Which AWS service is a managed container service that makes it easy to run Kubernetes on AWS without needing to install and operate your own Kubernetes control plane?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Redshift

options.label: D
options.text: AWS AppSync

explanation: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) is a managed service that you can use to run Kubernetes on AWS and on-premises data centers without needing to maintain your own Kubernetes control plane or nodes.

questionText: What is AWS Fargate?

options.label: A
options.text: A serverless compute engine for containers that works with both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS, eliminating the need to manage EC2 instances

options.label: B
options.text: A physical gateway device for connecting corporate LANs

options.label: C
options.text: A relational database proxy service

options.label: D
options.text: An interactive code repository hosting service

explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless, pay-as-you-go compute engine that lets you build applications without managing servers. Fargate runs containers for Amazon ECS and EKS without requiring you to manage EC2 instances or cluster capacity.

questionText: Where can Docker container images be stored, managed, and retrieved within AWS?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Artifact

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon FSx for Lustre

explanation: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) is a fully managed container registry that makes it easy for developers to store, manage, share, and deploy container images and artifacts anywhere.

questionText: Which of the following are serverless services on AWS? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Lambda

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon DynamoDB

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon EC2

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon RDS for Oracle

options.label: E
options.text: Amazon EMR with master node clusters

explanation: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB are classic serverless services that automatically scale, offer built-in high availability, and do not require provisioning, patching, or managing servers.

questionText: Which event source can directly trigger an AWS Lambda function execution? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: An object being uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket

options.label: B
options.text: A message arriving in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) queue

options.label: C
options.text: A monthly PDF billing invoice generated in the billing console

options.label: D
options.text: A user viewing their AWS Cost Explorer chart in a browser

options.label: E
options.text: A manual reboot of a home office broadband router

explanation: AWS Lambda can be natively triggered by events from over 200 AWS services, including S3 bucket uploads, DynamoDB streams, SQS messages, SNS notifications, API Gateway HTTP requests, and EventBridge events.

questionText: What is the primary operational difference between running Amazon ECS on EC2 launch type versus ECS on AWS Fargate?

options.label: A
options.text: With EC2 launch type you manage the underlying OS patching and server fleet; with Fargate AWS manages all server infrastructure serverlessly

options.label: B
options.text: EC2 launch type only supports Python, while Fargate only supports Java

options.label: C
options.text: Fargate requires purchasing physical hardware upfront

options.label: D
options.text: EC2 launch type does not support Docker containers

explanation: With ECS on EC2, you maintain and patch the virtual servers in the cluster. With AWS Fargate, you simply specify CPU and memory requirements and AWS runs the containers serverlessly without server management.

questionText: What is an AWS Lambda layer?

options.label: A
options.text: A distribution mechanism for libraries, custom runtimes, and other function dependencies to promote code reuse across multiple functions

options.label: B
options.text: A physical cooling rack inside an AWS data center

options.label: C
options.text: An encryption barrier between public and private subnets

options.label: D
options.text: A virtual private cloud peering connection

explanation: A Lambda layer is a .zip file archive that can contain additional code, libraries, pre-compiled binaries, or custom runtimes. Layers let you share common code across multiple Lambda functions without bloating deployment packages.

questionText: Which AWS service is an interactive visual workflow service used to orchestrate serverless architectures and coordinate multiple AWS Lambda functions?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Step Functions

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CodeBuild

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch

options.label: D
options.text: AWS App2Container

explanation: AWS Step Functions is a low-code visual workflow service used to orchestrate AWS services (such as AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, and Amazon DynamoDB) into business processes and distributed state machines.

questionText: Which compute model requires the customer to manage zero operating system patches, zero hardware updates, and zero server provisioning?

options.label: A
options.text: Serverless compute (e.g., AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate)

options.label: B
options.text: Infrastructure as a Service (e.g., Amazon EC2)

options.label: C
options.text: On-premises dedicated bare metal servers

options.label: D
options.text: Co-located server hosting in a private facility

explanation: In the serverless compute model (Lambda, Fargate), AWS handles all operating system maintenance, security patching, hardware provisioning, capacity scaling, and high availability.

questionText: A company wants to convert their legacy monolithic application into microservices packaged as container images. Which AWS services can manage the container deployments? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: E
options.text: Amazon Route 53 Resolver

explanation: Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS are AWS's two primary container orchestration services designed to deploy, run, and scale containerized microservices across cloud infrastructure.

questionText: What is an AWS Lambda cold start?

options.label: A
options.text: The initialization latency that occurs when a new execution environment is provisioned to handle an invocation for an inactive function

options.label: B
options.text: Shutting down servers during winter weather conditions

options.label: C
options.text: Starting an EC2 instance from an unformatted EBS volume

options.label: D
options.text: Restoring a database snapshot from cold tape storage

explanation: A cold start is the brief setup time that occurs when Lambda downloads your code, starts the container runtime, and initializes your code before executing an invocation on a freshly created execution environment.

questionText: Which feature of AWS Lambda eliminates cold start latency for critical production applications requiring consistent single-digit millisecond response times?

options.label: A
options.text: Provisioned Concurrency

options.label: B
options.text: Elastic Load Balancing health checks

options.label: C
options.text: Auto Scaling simple policies

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration

explanation: Provisioned Concurrency initializes a requested number of execution environments in advance so that they are prepared to respond immediately to function invocations with zero cold start latency.

questionText: Can AWS Lambda functions run inside a private Amazon VPC to access private RDS databases and internal services?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, by configuring VPC connectivity (subnets and security groups) in the Lambda function configuration

options.label: B
options.text: No, Lambda is strictly a public service and cannot connect to private VPC resources

options.label: C
options.text: Only if the database is open to 0.0.0.0/0 on the public Internet

options.label: D
options.text: Only when running on Dedicated EC2 Hosts

explanation: Lambda functions can be configured to connect to private subnets within your Amazon VPC, allowing secure access to internal resources like Amazon RDS databases, ElastiCache clusters, and private API endpoints.

questionText: Which container runtime is standardly supported by Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS)?

options.label: A
options.text: Docker

options.label: B
options.text: VMware vSphere hypervisor

options.label: C
options.text: Microsoft Hyper-V hardware virtualization

options.label: D
options.text: VirtualBox desktop manager

explanation: Amazon ECS is built to orchestrate Docker containers and OCI-compliant container formats, allowing standardized container packaging and execution.

questionText: What is a Task Definition in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)?

options.label: A
options.text: A text blueprint in JSON format that describes one or more containers (images, CPU, memory, ports) that form your application

options.label: B
options.text: A daily checklist for system administrators logged in Jira

options.label: C
options.text: A firewall rule defining inbound TCP traffic permissions

options.label: D
options.text: An AWS IAM user credential policy

explanation: An ECS Task Definition is a text blueprint in JSON format that details the containers that make up your application, including Docker image URLs, CPU and memory allocation, environment variables, and port mappings.

questionText: Which AWS service allows developers to write and test AWS Lambda functions directly within a browser-based Integrated Development Environment (IDE)?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cloud9

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CodeCommit

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon QuickSight

explanation: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based Integrated Development Environment (IDE) that lets you write, run, and debug code with just a browser. It comes prepackaged with essential tools for popular programming languages and AWS serverless development.

questionText: Which architectural pattern is best exemplified by AWS Lambda processing images immediately as they are uploaded to Amazon S3?

options.label: A
options.text: Event-driven architecture

options.label: B
options.text: Monolithic client-server architecture

options.label: C
options.text: Synchronous blocking batch loop

options.label: D
options.text: Peer-to-peer file sharing protocol

explanation: Event-driven architecture uses events to trigger and communicate between decoupled services. S3 notifying Lambda upon an S3 PutObject event is a textbook event-driven serverless design.

questionText: What is the maximum execution memory that can be allocated to an individual AWS Lambda function?

options.label: C
options.text: 512 MB

options.label: D
options.text: 64 GB

explanation: AWS Lambda functions can be allocated between 128 MB and 10,240 MB (10 GB) of memory in 1 MB increments. Lambda allocates CPU power proportionally to the amount of memory selected.

questionText: How does AWS Lambda automatically provide high availability?

options.label: A
options.text: By running execution environments across multiple Availability Zones in the chosen Region automatically

options.label: B
options.text: By duplicating code onto client mobile devices

options.label: C
options.text: By demanding the customer configure three standby EC2 servers

options.label: D
options.text: By restricting functions to run only during daytime hours

explanation: AWS Lambda is architected with built-in high availability across multiple Availability Zones in each AWS Region. Customers do not need to configure multi-AZ failover or redundant standby nodes.

questionText: Which AWS service is a managed pub/sub messaging and mobile push notification service that can trigger Lambda functions?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Route 53

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Aurora

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Storage Gateway

explanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub messaging service. When a message is published to an SNS topic, it can be fanned out to thousands of subscribers, including triggering AWS Lambda functions.

questionText: What is the primary advantage of containers compared to traditional virtual machines?

options.label: A
options.text: Containers share the host OS kernel and are lightweight, fast to spin up, and use fewer system resources than full virtual machines

options.label: B
options.text: Containers include an entire separate guest operating system inside every container

options.label: C
options.text: Containers are physical hardware cards inserted into PCIe slots

options.label: D
options.text: Containers eliminate all software vulnerabilities automatically

explanation: Containers package application code, configurations, and dependencies while sharing the host operating system kernel. This makes them significantly lighter, faster to boot, and more portable than traditional VMs.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group?

options.label: A
options.text: Automatically adjusting the number of EC2 instances up or down to maintain steady performance at the lowest possible cost

options.label: B
options.text: Automatically increasing the credit limit of your corporate credit card

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically updating domain name registrations every 30 days

options.label: D
options.text: Deleting database backups after 24 hours

explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling helps you maintain application availability and allows you to dynamically add or remove EC2 instances according to conditions you define (demand, schedule, or metrics).

questionText: Which scaling policy type adjusts Auto Scaling capacity to keep a specific metric (like average CPU utilization) at a specified target value (e.g., 60%)?

options.label: A
options.text: Target Tracking Scaling Policy

options.label: B
options.text: Simple Scaling Policy

options.label: C
options.text: Step Scaling Policy

options.label: D
options.text: Scheduled Scaling Policy

explanation: Target tracking scaling policies automatically adjust the capacity of your Auto Scaling group to maintain a target metric value (like keeping average aggregate CPU utilization at 60% or ALB request count per target at 1,000).

questionText: A company experiences predictable spikes in e-commerce traffic every Friday at 6 PM. Which EC2 Auto Scaling strategy is best suited to handle this known schedule?

options.label: A
options.text: Scheduled Scaling

options.label: B
options.text: Predictive Scaling with zero history

options.label: C
options.text: Manual rebooting of servers

options.label: D
options.text: Dynamic scaling based on disk space

explanation: Scheduled scaling allows you to set up your own scaling schedule based on predictable, recurring traffic patterns (such as weekly batch jobs or weekend retail promotions).

questionText: Which Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) type operates at the application layer (Layer 7) and supports path-based and host-based routing for HTTP and HTTPS traffic?

options.label: A
options.text: Application Load Balancer (ALB)

options.label: B
options.text: Network Load Balancer (NLB)

options.label: C
options.text: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)

options.label: D
options.text: Classic Load Balancer (CLB legacy)

explanation: Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 of the OSI model and supports advanced request routing based on URL paths (/api, /images), host headers, HTTP methods, and query strings.

questionText: Which Elastic Load Balancer type operates at the transport layer (Layer 4), is capable of handling millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, and supports static IP addresses?

options.label: A
options.text: Network Load Balancer (NLB)

options.label: B
options.text: Application Load Balancer (ALB)

options.label: C
options.text: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)

options.label: D
options.text: Route 53 latency policy

explanation: Network Load Balancer (NLB) operates at Layer 4 (TCP, UDP, TLS), offers ultra-high throughput with ultra-low latency, and provides a static IP per Availability Zone (or supports Elastic IPs).

questionText: Which load balancer is specifically designed to deploy, scale, and manage third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and deep packet inspection systems?

options.label: A
options.text: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)

options.label: B
options.text: Application Load Balancer (ALB)

options.label: C
options.text: Network Load Balancer (NLB)

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Direct Connect gateway

explanation: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) operates at Layer 3/4 and enables you to deploy, scale, and manage third-party virtual appliances such as next-generation firewalls (NGFW) and intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS).

questionText: What mechanism does Elastic Load Balancing use to verify whether registered targets (EC2 instances or containers) are operational before routing client traffic to them?

options.label: A
options.text: Health Checks

options.label: B
options.text: IAM policy audits

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor cost reports

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Billing alerts

explanation: Elastic Load Balancing periodically performs health checks against registered targets. If a target fails consecutive health checks, the load balancer stops routing traffic to that unhealthy target until it becomes healthy again.

questionText: What are the three core capacity parameters configured on an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group?

options.label: A
options.text: Minimum capacity, Maximum capacity, and Desired capacity

options.label: B
options.text: Primary capacity, Secondary capacity, and Standby capacity

options.label: C
options.text: Single capacity, Double capacity, and Triple capacity

options.label: D
options.text: Local capacity, Regional capacity, and Global capacity

explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling group is defined by: 1) Minimum capacity (lowest instance count permitted), 2) Maximum capacity (upper ceiling to cap cost), and 3) Desired capacity (target instance count maintained during normal operation).

questionText: What is an EC2 Launch Template?

options.label: A
options.text: A version-controlled specification that defines instance configuration details (AMI ID, instance type, key pair, security groups, block device mapping) used by Auto Scaling

options.label: B
options.text: A paper questionnaire mailed to AWS support to request hardware

options.label: C
options.text: A CloudWatch alarm that alerts on disk saturation

options.label: D
options.text: A pricing spreadsheet used by financial controllers

explanation: A Launch Template specifies instance configuration information. It supports versioning, allows partial parameter definitions, and is the modern replacement for legacy Launch Configurations in EC2 Auto Scaling.

questionText: What happens when an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group fails an ELB health check?

options.label: A
options.text: The Auto Scaling group marks the instance as unhealthy, terminates it, and launches a healthy replacement instance

options.label: B
options.text: The instance is placed in hibernation for 30 days

options.label: C
options.text: The entire VPC is deleted automatically

options.label: D
options.text: AWS sends an engineer to replace the physical RAM in the server

explanation: When ELB health check integration is enabled on an Auto Scaling group, if an instance fails ELB health checks, the Auto Scaling group terminates the unhealthy instance and launches a new healthy replacement to maintain desired capacity.

questionText: What is the purpose of Auto Scaling Cooldown periods?

options.label: A
options.text: To ensure that the Auto Scaling group does not launch or terminate additional instances before the previous scaling activity takes effect and metrics stabilize

options.label: B
options.text: To cool down server CPUs with chilled water in the data center

options.label: C
options.text: To allow administrators to take a mandatory break during exams

options.label: D
options.text: To prevent billing invoices from being generated

explanation: A cooldown period is a configurable amount of time during which the Auto Scaling group suspends additional scaling activities, ensuring the group doesn't overcompensate before newly launched instances stabilize.

questionText: How does an Application Load Balancer distribute traffic across multiple Availability Zones?

options.label: A
options.text: By registering targets across subnets in multiple AZs and using cross-zone load balancing to route traffic evenly

options.label: B
options.text: By duplicating every single incoming HTTP packet to all instances in parallel

options.label: C
options.text: By routing traffic only to the AZ that has the lowest ambient room temperature

options.label: D
options.text: By sending all traffic to one AZ until that data center experiences a physical blackout

explanation: When an ALB is configured across multiple Availability Zones, cross-zone load balancing ensures requests are distributed evenly across all registered targets in all enabled AZs, maximizing fault tolerance and resilience.

questionText: Which load balancer feature directs a user's consecutive requests to the same target instance for session state persistence?

options.label: A
options.text: Sticky Sessions (Session Affinity)

options.label: B
options.text: Connection Draining

options.label: C
options.text: Path-Based Routing

options.label: D
options.text: DNS Round-Robin

explanation: Sticky Sessions (Session Affinity) binds a user's session to a specific target instance behind the load balancer using HTTP cookies, ensuring stateful session data stored in server memory remains reachable by the user.

questionText: What is Connection Draining (Deregistration Delay) in Elastic Load Balancing?

options.label: A
options.text: A feature that allows in-flight requests to complete before an instance is de-registered or terminated

options.label: B
options.text: Flushing unused network cables in the data center

options.label: C
options.text: Disconnecting database connection pools during backup windows

options.label: D
options.text: Immediately dropping all user connections when an instance is marked unhealthy

explanation: Connection Draining (Deregistration Delay) ensures that the load balancer stops sending new requests to de-registering instances while allowing existing, in-flight requests to complete gracefully within a specified timeout.

questionText: Which Auto Scaling feature uses machine learning to forecast future compute traffic based on past patterns and provisions capacity ahead of anticipated spikes?

options.label: A
options.text: Predictive Scaling

options.label: B
options.text: Manual Scaling

options.label: C
options.text: Simple Scaling

options.label: D
options.text: Step Scaling

explanation: Predictive Scaling uses machine learning models to analyze historical traffic patterns and forecast upcoming capacity needs, scheduling instance scaling actions ahead of time so capacity is ready before traffic arrives.

questionText: Can an Auto Scaling group span across multiple AWS Regions?

options.label: A
options.text: No, an Auto Scaling group can span multiple Availability Zones within a single Region, but cannot span multiple Regions

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, a single Auto Scaling group automatically spans all global AWS regions

options.label: C
options.text: Only if AWS Organizations consolidated billing is active

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, if configured through AWS Route 53

explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling group is a regional construct: it can span multiple Availability Zones within the same AWS Region, but it cannot span multiple separate AWS Regions.

questionText: Which protocol types are supported by an Application Load Balancer?

options.label: A
options.text: HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, and WebSockets

options.label: B
options.text: Raw TCP and UDP exclusively

options.label: C
options.text: FTP and SMTP email transmission only

options.label: D
options.text: BGP and ICMP ping packets exclusively

explanation: Application Load Balancer is engineered for application traffic and natively supports HTTP, HTTPS, WebSockets, and gRPC protocols at Layer 7 of the OSI stack.

questionText: Which load balancer should you use if your application requires a single fixed, static public IP address for clients with strict firewall whitelisting?

options.label: A
options.text: Network Load Balancer (NLB)

options.label: B
options.text: Application Load Balancer (ALB)

options.label: C
options.text: Classic Load Balancer (CLB)

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Route 53 failover record

explanation: Network Load Balancers provide a static IP address per Availability Zone (and support assigning Elastic IPs). In contrast, ALBs only provide DNS names whose IP addresses change dynamically.

questionText: How do Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing combine to support the Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.label: A
options.text: ELB distributes traffic across healthy targets while Auto Scaling replaces failed instances and scales capacity to match demand

options.label: B
options.text: They convert all relational databases into flat text files automatically

options.label: C
options.text: They eliminate the requirement for data encryption at rest

options.label: D
options.text: They guarantee 100% discount on all compute costs

explanation: Together, ELB routes traffic only to healthy instances across multiple AZs while Auto Scaling automatically detects failures, replaces unhealthy instances, and dynamically scales capacity, delivering high availability and fault tolerance.

questionText: What is an Auto Scaling Lifecycle Hook?

options.label: A
options.text: A feature that pauses the launch or termination of an instance to perform custom actions (like log extraction or software setup) before entering or exiting service

options.label: B
options.text: A phishing detection tool in Amazon GuardDuty

options.label: C
options.text: A webhook that notifies billing controllers when invoices are overdue

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware clip for rack-mounting servers in Outposts

explanation: Lifecycle Hooks let you pause an instance as it launches or terminates, allowing you to perform custom actions (e.g., installing software, running health scripts, or backing up state/logs) before the instance is put in service or destroyed.

questionText: What is an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)?

options.label: A
options.text: A logically isolated virtual network dedicated to your AWS account within the AWS cloud

options.label: B
options.text: A physical cable connecting your office router to an AWS data center

options.label: C
options.text: A software development kit for building mobile apps

options.label: D
options.text: A public file storage repository open to all Internet users

explanation: Amazon VPC lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a virtual network that you define, with complete control over IP addressing, subnets, and routing.

questionText: What distinguishes a public subnet from a private subnet in an Amazon VPC?

options.label: A
options.text: A public subnet has a direct route to an Internet Gateway (IGW) in its route table; a private subnet does not

options.label: B
options.text: Public subnets use IPv6, while private subnets use IPv4

options.label: C
options.text: Public subnets do not support EC2 instances

options.label: D
options.text: Private subnets are located outside the AWS Region

explanation: A public subnet is a subnet whose associated route table contains a default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to an Internet Gateway (IGW). A private subnet lacks a direct route to the Internet Gateway, isolating its instances from inbound Internet traffic.

questionText: Which component enables instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound traffic to the Internet (for software updates) while preventing the Internet from initiating inbound connections?

options.label: A
options.text: NAT Gateway (or NAT Instance)

options.label: B
options.text: Internet Gateway (IGW)

options.label: C
options.text: Customer Gateway

options.label: D
options.text: Virtual Private Gateway

explanation: A Network Address Translation (NAT) Gateway is placed in a public subnet to allow instances in private subnets to send outbound requests to the Internet (e.g., OS updates) while blocking external inbound connections.

questionText: What is the primary difference between a Security Group and a Network Access Control List (NACL)?

options.label: A
options.text: Security Groups operate at the instance level and are stateful; NACLs operate at the subnet level and are stateless

options.label: B
options.text: Security Groups operate at the subnet level; NACLs operate at the account root level

options.label: C
options.text: Security Groups support deny rules; NACLs only support allow rules

options.label: D
options.text: Security Groups are stateless; NACLs are stateful

explanation: Security Groups act as a virtual firewall for individual instances and are stateful (return traffic is automatically allowed). Network ACLs act at the subnet boundary, are stateless (inbound and outbound rules must be explicitly defined), and evaluate numbered allow/deny rules in order.

questionText: Which statement is true about Security Group rules?

options.label: A
options.text: They allow you to specify allow rules only; you cannot write explicit deny rules

options.label: B
options.text: They evaluate deny rules before allow rules

options.label: C
options.text: They block all outbound traffic by default and cannot be changed

options.label: D
options.text: They are evaluated strictly in sequential numerical rule order

explanation: Security Groups only support ALLOW rules. All traffic not explicitly allowed is denied by default. To explicitly deny traffic from a specific IP address, you must use a Network ACL (NACL).

questionText: What is Amazon Route 53?

options.label: A
options.text: A highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service

options.label: B
options.text: A physical highway navigation device provided by AWS

options.label: C
options.text: An automated road freight tracking system

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware router deployed at branch offices

explanation: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service. It translates human-friendly names (like www.example.com) into numeric IP addresses (like 192.0.2.1).

questionText: Which Route 53 routing policy routes user requests to the AWS endpoint that provides the lowest network latency for the end user?

options.label: A
options.text: Latency Routing Policy

options.label: B
options.text: Failover Routing Policy

options.label: C
options.text: Weighted Routing Policy

options.label: D
options.text: Geolocation Routing Policy

explanation: Route 53 Latency-based routing directs traffic to the AWS Region that provides the lowest round-trip network latency for the user, based on worldwide network measurements.

questionText: Which Route 53 routing policy allows you to route traffic based on the geographic location of your users (by country or continent)?

options.label: A
options.text: Geolocation Routing Policy

options.label: B
options.text: Multivalue Answer Routing Policy

options.label: C
options.text: Simple Routing Policy

options.label: D
options.text: IP-based Routing Policy

explanation: Geolocation routing lets you choose the resources that serve your traffic based on the geographic location of your users (continent, country, or US state), ideal for localized content or licensing compliance.

questionText: What is Amazon CloudFront?

options.label: A
options.text: A fast, secure Content Delivery Network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to global customers with low latency

options.label: B
options.text: A weather forecasting tool used by meteorological agencies

options.label: C
options.text: A desktop file explorer client for Windows

options.label: D
options.text: A physical server shipped to customer premises for cold storage

explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a fast Content Delivery Network (CDN) service that caches and delivers static and dynamic content through a worldwide network of edge locations, accelerating delivery and reducing load on origin servers.

questionText: Which AWS service establishes a dedicated, private physical network connection from an on-premises data center directly to AWS, bypassing the public Internet entirely?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Route 53 Resolver

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Global Accelerator

explanation: AWS Direct Connect links your internal on-premises network to an AWS Direct Connect location over a standard Ethernet fiber-optic cable, bypassing the public Internet to deliver consistent performance, higher bandwidth, and reduced data egress costs.

questionText: What is the primary difference between AWS Direct Connect and AWS Site-to-Site VPN?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct Connect is a dedicated private physical circuit bypassing the Internet; Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted IPsec tunnel over the public Internet

options.label: B
options.text: Site-to-Site VPN requires 6 months of physical cable construction; Direct Connect is instant software

options.label: C
options.text: Direct Connect is free, while Site-to-Site VPN costs millions of dollars per month

options.label: D
options.text: There is no functional difference between them

explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted IPSec connection over the public Internet that can be set up in minutes. AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, non-Internet physical telecommunications circuit providing higher throughput and predictable latency.

questionText: What is a VPC Peering connection?

options.label: A
options.text: A networking connection between two VPCs that enables you to route traffic between them using private IPv4 or IPv6 addresses

options.label: B
options.text: A public video conference channel between AWS customer support engineers

options.label: C
options.text: A shared root account between two distinct companies

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware bridge connecting two consumer laptops via USB

explanation: A VPC peering connection is a networking connection between two VPCs that enables you to route traffic between them using private IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. Instances in either VPC can communicate with each other as if they are within the same network.

questionText: Is VPC peering transitive?

options.label: A
options.text: No, VPC peering is non-transitive (if VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B is peered with VPC C, VPC A cannot communicate with VPC C through B)

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, all VPC peering connections automatically route traffic across all other peered VPCs globally

options.label: C
options.text: Only if both VPCs are in the same Availability Zone

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, provided the CIDR blocks are completely identical

explanation: VPC Peering does NOT support transitive routing. If VPC A is connected to VPC B, and VPC B is connected to VPC C, you cannot route traffic from VPC A to VPC C through VPC B; you must create an explicit peering connection between A and C (or use AWS Transit Gateway).

questionText: Which service acts as a central cloud router hub to connect hundreds of VPCs and on-premises networks together without complex point-to-point peering meshes?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Transit Gateway

options.label: B
options.text: Internet Gateway

options.label: C
options.text: NAT Instance

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

explanation: AWS Transit Gateway connects thousands of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub. This simplifies network topology and eliminates the need for complex, pairwise point-to-point VPC peering connections.

questionText: What is AWS Global Accelerator?

options.label: A
options.text: A networking service that improves the availability and performance of applications by directing user traffic through the AWS global private network using static Anycast IP addresses

options.label: B
options.text: A hardware overclocking utility for EC2 CPU processors

options.label: C
options.text: A startup incubator funding grant provided by Amazon

options.label: D
options.text: A continuous delivery pipeline automation server

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator uses AWS's global network backbone to route traffic from users to your application endpoints via two static Anycast IP addresses, providing up to 60% performance improvement and fast regional failover.

questionText: What is an AWS VPC Endpoint?

options.label: A
options.text: A private virtual device that enables private connections between your VPC and supported AWS services without requiring an Internet Gateway or NAT Gateway

options.label: B
options.text: A physical termination box at the boundary of a data center

options.label: C
options.text: A wireless access point for office employees

options.label: D
options.text: A software agent installed on mobile phones

explanation: VPC Endpoints allow you to privately connect your VPC to supported AWS services (like Amazon S3, DynamoDB) and VPC endpoint services powered by AWS PrivateLink without requiring an Internet Gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect.

questionText: What are the two types of VPC Endpoints?

options.label: A
options.text: Interface Endpoints (powered by PrivateLink with an ENI) and Gateway Endpoints (used for S3 and DynamoDB)

options.label: B
options.text: Public Endpoints and Commercial Endpoints

options.label: C
options.text: Hardware Endpoints and Virtual Endpoints

options.label: D
options.text: Encrypted Endpoints and Unencrypted Endpoints

explanation: The two types of VPC Endpoints are: 1) Gateway Endpoints (free, target routes in route tables for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB), and 2) Interface Endpoints (elastic network interfaces with private IP addresses powered by AWS PrivateLink for most other AWS services).

questionText: What does CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) represent in an Amazon VPC?

options.label: A
options.text: The Classless Inter-Domain Routing range of private IPv4 addresses allocated to the VPC

options.label: B
options.text: The geographic coordinate of the physical data center

options.label: C
options.text: The monthly dollar budget allocated to the network team

options.label: D
options.text: The version number of the AWS management API

explanation: Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation defines the range of private IPv4 addresses available to resources within the VPC (e.g., /16 provides 65,536 available IP addresses).

questionText: How many IP addresses does AWS reserve for internal networking purposes in every VPC subnet?

options.label: A
options.text: 5 IP addresses (first 4 and the last 1 in the subnet range)

options.label: B
options.text: 0 IP addresses (all are available to the customer)

options.label: C
options.text: 10 IP addresses

options.label: D
options.text: 1 IP address

explanation: In every VPC subnet, AWS reserves the first four IP addresses and the last IP address (e.g., .0 Network, .1 Router, .2 DNS, .3 Future use, and .255 Broadcast), making them unavailable for customer instance assignment.

questionText: What is the primary function of VPC Flow Logs?

options.label: A
options.text: To capture information about the IP address traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC for monitoring, troubleshooting, and security audits

options.label: B
options.text: To measure the physical temperature of network switches

options.label: C
options.text: To record video streams of administrators logging into the console

options.label: D
options.text: To automatically compress image files uploaded to S3

explanation: VPC Flow Logs enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. Flow log data can be published to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for analysis.

questionText: Which Route 53 record type allows you to map a root domain (zone apex, e.g., example.com) directly to an AWS resource like an Application Load Balancer or CloudFront distribution?

options.label: A
options.text: Alias Record

options.label: B
options.text: CNAME Record

options.label: C
options.text: PTR Record

options.label: D
options.text: TXT Record

explanation: Route 53 Alias records are AWS-specific extensions to DNS that let you map zone apex domain names directly to AWS resources (ALBs, CloudFront, S3 buckets) while automatically recognizing IP address changes and avoiding DNS query charges.

questionText: Why cannot standard DNS CNAME records be used at the zone apex (e.g., example.com)?

options.label: A
options.text: DNS standards (RFC) forbid CNAME records at the root domain level, which is why Route 53 Alias records are used

options.label: B
options.text: AWS billing rules impose a penalty on CNAME records

options.label: C
options.text: CNAME records only work on local internal networks

options.label: D
options.text: CNAME records do not support HTTPS encryption

explanation: Under DNS RFC specifications, a CNAME record cannot coexist with other record types (like SOA and NS records) at the zone apex (root domain). Route 53 Alias records solve this problem by resolving natively at the apex.

questionText: Which service provides origin shielding and caching to protect your origin servers from high traffic volumes?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon CloudFront

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowball Edge

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon QuickSight

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Budgets

explanation: Amazon CloudFront acts as a caching reverse proxy. When content is cached at edge locations and regional edge caches, requests are served directly from the cache, shielding the origin server from traffic spikes.

questionText: An application needs to block incoming requests originating from specific malicious IP addresses identified during a security scan. Which VPC feature can implement explicit DENY rules?

options.label: A
options.text: Network Access Control List (NACL)

options.label: B
options.text: Security Group

options.label: C
options.text: NAT Gateway

options.label: D
options.text: Internet Gateway

explanation: Network ACLs support numbered rules that evaluate allow and deny statements in order. To explicitly block a specific IP address or CIDR block, you add a DENY rule to the inbound NACL table.

questionText: What is a Customer Gateway in an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection?

options.label: A
options.text: An anchor on the on-premises side of the VPN connection (a physical appliance or software application)

options.label: B
options.text: The AWS-managed VPN endpoint inside the VPC

options.label: C
options.text: A retail store checkout counter for AWS hardware

options.label: D
options.text: A billing portal for corporate customers

explanation: In an AWS Site-to-Site VPN, the Customer Gateway is the physical device or software appliance on your on-premises side of the connection. The Virtual Private Gateway (or Transit Gateway) is the anchor on the AWS side.

questionText: What is an AWS Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)?

options.label: A
options.text: The VPN concentrator on the AWS side of a Site-to-Site VPN or Direct Connect connection attached to your VPC

options.label: B
options.text: An email spam filter on AWS

options.label: C
options.text: A dedicated physical firewall shipped to corporate offices

options.label: D
options.text: A web browser extension developed by AWS

explanation: A Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) is the virtual VPN concentrator attached to your VPC that serves as the AWS target endpoint for Site-to-Site VPN connections and AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces.

questionText: Which Route 53 health checking feature can automatically redirect traffic away from an unhealthy server to a healthy standby server in another region?

options.label: A
options.text: DNS Failover Routing with Route 53 Health Checks

options.label: B
options.text: EBS volume snapshot cloning

options.label: C
options.text: IAM credential cycling

options.label: D
options.text: S3 standard versioning

explanation: Route 53 DNS Failover uses periodic health checks against your application endpoints. If the primary endpoint fails health checks, Route 53 automatically updates DNS responses to route users to a healthy backup endpoint.

questionText: What does AWS PrivateLink provide?

options.label: A
options.text: Private, secure connectivity between VPCs, supported AWS services, and on-premises networks without exposing traffic to the public Internet

options.label: B
options.text: A free Wi-Fi hotspot in Amazon fulfillment centers

options.label: C
options.text: An encrypted peer-to-peer file sharing protocol

options.label: D
options.text: A social networking service for cloud architects

explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs, AWS services, and on-premises networks using interface VPC endpoints and private IP addresses, ensuring traffic never traverses the public Internet.

questionText: Which AWS network service can be paired with Amazon CloudFront to inspect HTTP/HTTPS web requests and block SQL injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Shield Advanced without rules

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Route 53 Resolver

explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that lets you monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests forwarded to Amazon CloudFront, Application Load Balancers, or API Gateway, and block attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS).

questionText: What is an Internet Gateway (IGW) in Amazon VPC?

options.label: A
options.text: A horizontally scaled, redundant, highly available VPC component that enables communication between instances in your VPC and the Internet

options.label: B
options.text: A physical modem plugged into an EC2 server

options.label: C
options.text: An encryption appliance that terminates SSH sessions

options.label: D
options.text: A software proxy installed inside the operating system

explanation: An Internet Gateway (IGW) is a horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available VPC component that allows communication between your VPC and the Internet without availability risks or bandwidth constraints.

questionText: What type of storage is Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)?

options.label: A
options.text: Object storage

options.label: B
options.text: Block storage

options.label: C
options.text: File system storage

options.label: D
options.text: Tape physical drive

explanation: Amazon S3 is an object storage service that stores data as objects within buckets, providing industry-leading scalability, data availability, security, and performance.

questionText: What is the designed durability of objects stored in Amazon S3 Standard?
explanation: Amazon S3 Standard is designed to deliver 99.999999999% (11 nines) of data durability over a given year by redundantly storing data across multiple physically separated Availability Zones.

questionText: Which Amazon S3 storage class is best suited for data with unknown or changing access patterns, automatically shifting objects between access tiers without operational overhead or retrieval fees?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering

options.label: B
options.text: S3 Standard-IA

options.label: C
options.text: S3 One Zone-IA

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive

explanation: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the only cloud storage class that delivers automatic cost savings by moving objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive access tiers when access patterns change, with zero retrieval fees.

questionText: Which S3 storage class provides the lowest-cost storage in AWS for long-term data retention and compliance archives that can tolerate retrieval times of 9 to 12 hours?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Standard

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon S3 One Zone-IA

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon S3 Express One Zone

explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is Amazon S3's lowest-cost storage tier, designed for long-term retention and digital preservation of data that is accessed once or twice a year, with retrieval times typically within 12 hours.

questionText: A company wants to store secondary, easily reproducible backup data at a lower cost than S3 Standard-IA. They do not require multi-AZ redundancy. Which storage class is suitable?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon S3 One Zone-IA

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon S3 Standard

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Elastic File System

explanation: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone at a 20% lower cost than S3 Standard-IA. It is ideal for reproducible data or secondary copies that do not require multi-AZ resilience against physical disaster.

questionText: What is the maximum size of a single object that can be stored in an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.label: A
options.text: 5 Terabytes (5 TB)

options.label: B
options.text: 5 Gigabytes (5 GB)

options.label: C
options.text: 100 Terabytes

options.label: D
options.text: Unlimited size for a single object

explanation: The total volume of data and number of objects in an S3 bucket are unlimited, but individual Amazon S3 objects can range in size from a minimum of 0 bytes up to a maximum of 5 TB.

questionText: Which Amazon S3 feature enables you to automatically transition objects between storage classes or expire them after a defined period of time?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 Lifecycle Policies

options.label: B
options.text: S3 Versioning

options.label: C
options.text: S3 Object Lock

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Batch Operations

explanation: S3 Lifecycle management rules automatically transition objects between different storage classes (e.g., Standard to Standard-IA after 30 days, then to Glacier after 90 days) or expire/delete them to optimize storage costs over time.

questionText: What does Amazon S3 Versioning do?

options.label: A
options.text: Keeps multiple historical variants of an object in the same bucket, protecting against accidental overwrites or deletions

options.label: B
options.text: Upgrades the software version of your EC2 instances

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically edits source code repositories

options.label: D
options.text: Translates document text into multiple foreign languages

explanation: S3 Versioning preserves, retrieves, and restores every version of every object stored in your Amazon S3 bucket, allowing easy recovery from unintended user actions and application failures.

questionText: Which S3 feature enforces Write Once, Read Many (WORM) storage to prevent objects from being deleted or overwritten for a fixed retention period or indefinitely?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 Object Lock

options.label: B
options.text: S3 Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

options.label: C
options.text: S3 Multipart Upload

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Event Notifications

explanation: S3 Object Lock enables you to store objects using a WORM model. It prevents an object from being deleted or overwritten for a fixed amount of time or indefinitely, helping satisfy regulatory compliance (like SEC Rule 17a-4).

questionText: What type of storage is Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)?

options.label: A
options.text: Persistent block-level storage designed for use with Amazon EC2 instances

options.label: B
options.text: Object storage accessed exclusively over public HTTP REST APIs

options.label: C
options.text: Shared distributed cloud network file system for thousands of Linux instances

options.label: D
options.text: Magnetic tape library for long-term cold storage

explanation: Amazon EBS provides block-level storage volumes for use with EC2 instances. EBS volumes behave like raw, unformatted physical hard drives or SSDs that can be formatted with any file system.

questionText: Can a standard Amazon EBS volume be attached to an EC2 instance in a different Availability Zone from where the volume was created?
