options.label: A
options.text: No, an EBS volume is locked to a specific Availability Zone and can only be attached to instances in that same AZ

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, standard EBS volumes can be attached to instances in any AZ or Region

options.label: C
options.text: Only if the instance is a Spot Instance

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, through AWS Direct Connect

explanation: An EBS volume is physically located in a specific Availability Zone where it is automatically replicated to protect from component failure. To attach it to an EC2 instance, the instance must reside in that exact same AZ.

questionText: How can you migrate or copy an Amazon EBS volume to another Availability Zone or another AWS Region?

options.label: A
options.text: Take an EBS snapshot (stored in S3), copy the snapshot to the target AZ or Region, and create a new EBS volume from it

options.label: B
options.text: Use an FTP connection between the two physical servers

options.label: C
options.text: Unplug the physical hard drive and mail it via AWS Snowball

options.label: D
options.text: EBS volumes cannot be moved or copied under any circumstances

explanation: EBS Snapshots are point-in-time backups saved to Amazon S3. You can copy snapshots to other Availability Zones or other Regions, and then restore new EBS volumes from those snapshots in the target location.

questionText: What is the primary difference between Amazon EBS and EC2 Instance Store?

options.label: A
options.text: EBS is persistent independent block storage that survives instance stops; Instance Store is temporary ephemeral storage that is wiped when the instance stops

options.label: B
options.text: Instance store persists data forever, whereas EBS deletes all data upon instance reboot

options.label: C
options.text: EBS is free of charge, while Instance Store is billed per gigabyte per minute

options.label: D
options.text: Instance store is an object storage service accessed via REST APIs

explanation: EBS volumes persist independently of the life of an EC2 instance. Instance Store is physically attached to the host computer, providing ultra-low latency, but is ephemeral—data is permanently lost when the instance is stopped or terminated.

questionText: Which Amazon EBS volume type is designed for mission-critical, I/O intensive database workloads requiring sub-millisecond latency and sustained IOPS performance?

options.label: A
options.text: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 / io1)

options.label: B
options.text: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)

options.label: C
options.text: Cold HDD (sc1)

options.label: D
options.text: General Purpose SSD (gp2)

explanation: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express and io1) volumes are engineered to meet the needs of I/O-intensive workloads, particularly mission-critical database workloads sensitive to storage performance and consistency.

questionText: Which Amazon EBS volume type offers the lowest-cost HDD storage for infrequently accessed, throughput-oriented big data workloads and log processing?

options.label: A
options.text: Cold HDD (sc1)

options.label: B
options.text: General Purpose SSD (gp3)

options.label: C
options.text: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)

options.label: D
options.text: EBS Magnetic (standard)

explanation: Cold HDD (sc1) volumes provide the lowest-cost magnetic storage for throughput-oriented workloads with large datasets and infrequent access, such as big data cold storage and log consolidation.

questionText: What is Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)?

options.label: A
options.text: A serverless, fully managed, scalable Network File System (NFS) that can be mounted concurrently by hundreds of Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs

options.label: B
options.text: A Windows-only SMB file server requiring active directory management

options.label: C
options.text: A local SSD drive physically connected to an individual motherboard

options.label: D
options.text: A cold tape archival service

explanation: Amazon EFS provides a simple, serverless, set-and-forget elastic file system using the NFSv4 protocol. It automatically grows and shrinks as files are added and removed and can be mounted concurrently by thousands of Linux instances.

questionText: What is the key architectural difference between Amazon EBS and Amazon EFS regarding multi-instance concurrency?

options.label: A
options.text: Standard EBS volumes are typically mounted by a single instance in a single AZ; EFS can be mounted simultaneously by hundreds of instances across multiple AZs

options.label: B
options.text: EBS can be mounted by thousands of instances globally; EFS is strictly locked to one single instance

options.label: C
options.text: EFS cannot store files larger than 1 megabyte

options.label: D
options.text: EBS is managed file storage, while EFS is raw block storage

explanation: Amazon EBS is block storage designed primarily for a single instance in a single AZ. Amazon EFS is managed file storage (NFS) that can be shared concurrently across hundreds of compute instances running in multiple Availability Zones.

questionText: Which AWS managed file storage service is optimized for Windows-based applications requiring native SMB protocol support and full Microsoft Active Directory integration?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon S3 Express One Zone

options.label: D
options.text: AWS DataSync

explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed shared storage built on Windows Server, delivering full compatibility with Windows SMB protocols, Active Directory integration, NTFS permissions, and DFS.

questionText: Which AWS storage service is designed for compute-intensive workloads such as High Performance Computing (HPC), machine learning training, and financial modeling requiring sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of gigabytes per second throughput?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon FSx for Lustre

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon EBS Cold HDD

explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for fast processing of workloads such as machine learning, high performance computing (HPC), video processing, and financial modeling, delivering million-level IOPS and sub-millisecond latencies.

questionText: What is AWS Storage Gateway?

options.label: A
options.text: A hybrid cloud storage service that gives on-premises applications access to virtually unlimited AWS cloud storage (S3, EBS, Glacier)

options.label: B
options.text: A physical revolving turnstile for entering an AWS data center

options.label: C
options.text: A web browser plugin for downloading PDFs

options.label: D
options.text: A dedicated fiber optic line replacing local telecommunications

explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service that connects on-premises software appliances with cloud-based storage, providing seamless and secure data integration between your on-premises IT environment and AWS.

questionText: What are the three primary types of AWS Storage Gateway?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 File Gateway, Volume Gateway (Stored & Cached volumes), and Tape Gateway

options.label: B
options.text: Block Gateway, Container Gateway, and Serverless Gateway

options.label: C
options.text: Database Gateway, Compute Gateway, and Monitoring Gateway

options.label: D
options.text: Public Gateway, Private Gateway, and Hybrid Gateway

explanation: AWS Storage Gateway offers: 1) S3 File Gateway (file interface to S3), 2) Volume Gateway (cached or stored block volumes backed by EBS snapshots), and 3) Tape Gateway (virtual tape library replacing physical tape drives with S3 Glacier).

questionText: Which AWS Snow Family appliance allows you to transfer up to 80 Terabytes of on-premises data to AWS via a ruggedized physical shipping container?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowcone (8 TB)

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Snowmobile (up to 100 PB)

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

explanation: AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized provides up to 80 TB of usable block storage or S3-compatible object storage in a tamper-resistant, secure physical appliance shipped to your location for offline bulk data transfer.

questionText: Which member of the AWS Snow Family is designed to migrate exabyte-scale data sets (up to 100 Petabytes per unit) using a 45-foot ruggedized shipping container pulled by a semi-trailer truck?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Snowmobile

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowball Edge

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Snowcone

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Outposts

explanation: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data migration service used to move extremely large amounts of data to AWS. A 45-foot long ruggedized shipping container pulled by a semi-trailer truck can transfer up to 100 PB per Snowmobile.

questionText: Which AWS Snow Family device is the smallest and most portable, weighing only 4.5 lbs and capable of being deployed in edge or disconnected tactical environments?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Snowcone

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowball

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Snowmobile

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Storage Gateway

explanation: AWS Snowcone is the smallest member of the AWS Snow Family of edge computing, edge storage, and data transfer devices, weighing 4.5 lbs (2.1 kg) with 8 TB of usable storage.

questionText: What is S3 Transfer Acceleration?

options.label: A
options.text: A feature that speeds up long-distance uploads to S3 buckets by routing traffic through AWS Edge Locations over the AWS private network backbone

options.label: B
options.text: A tool that physically overclocks hard disk rotational speeds in data centers

options.label: C
options.text: A paid expedited delivery service for Snowball appliances

options.label: D
options.text: A compression utility that reduces image file sizes by 90%

explanation: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration enables fast, easy, and secure transfers of files over long distances between your client and an S3 bucket by routing uploads through Amazon CloudFront's globally distributed Edge Locations.

questionText: Which S3 feature allows you to replicate objects automatically across different AWS accounts and different AWS Regions for disaster recovery?

options.label: A
options.text: Cross-Region Replication (CRR)

options.label: B
options.text: Same-Region Replication (SRR)

options.label: C
options.text: S3 Select

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Storage Lens

explanation: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) automatically copies objects asynchronously across S3 buckets in different AWS Regions, enabling disaster recovery, compliance, and latency-optimized access for globally distributed users.

questionText: Can Amazon S3 host a static website containing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and client-side scripts?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, S3 natively supports static website hosting without requiring web servers like Apache or NGINX

options.label: B
options.text: No, S3 can only store binary backups and raw media files

options.label: C
options.text: Only if an EC2 instance is running inside the S3 bucket

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but it requires writing server-side PHP scripts

explanation: Amazon S3 can host static websites (HTML, images, CSS, client-side JavaScript). Static websites do not require server-side technologies (such as PHP, Python, or ASP.NET) and scale automatically to handle millions of visitors.

questionText: What is an S3 Bucket Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A resource-based IAM policy attached directly to an S3 bucket that grants permissions to the bucket and its objects

options.label: B
options.text: A billing contract signed when creating an AWS account

options.label: C
options.text: A legal disclaimer shown to website visitors

options.label: D
options.text: A firewall rule configured on a virtual router

explanation: An S3 Bucket Policy is a resource-based policy written in JSON format that you attach directly to an S3 bucket to specify which principals (users, accounts, or services) are allowed or denied actions on the bucket.

questionText: Which feature in Amazon S3 provides centralized organization-wide visibility into object storage usage, activity trends, and cost-optimization recommendations?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon S3 Storage Lens

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon S3 Inventory

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Artifact

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

explanation: Amazon S3 Storage Lens is a cloud storage analytics feature that delivers organization-wide visibility into object storage usage and activity trends, and provides actionable recommendations to optimize costs and security.

questionText: What is the primary benefit of EBS Elastic Volumes?

options.label: A
options.text: You can increase volume size, adjust performance (IOPS), and change volume types dynamically on the fly with zero downtime

options.label: B
options.text: They stretch physically across multiple server racks using rubber bands

options.label: C
options.text: They automatically delete older files when capacity reaches 90%

options.label: D
options.text: They are 100% free of charge regardless of volume size

explanation: EBS Elastic Volumes allow you to dynamically modify volume size, IOPS capacity, and volume type on live production volumes without detaching the volume or restarting the EC2 instance, ensuring continuous operations.

questionText: What is Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service)?

options.label: A
options.text: A managed web service that makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale relational databases in the AWS cloud

options.label: B
options.text: A key-value document store for gaming leaderboards

options.label: C
options.text: A graph database for mapping social network friendships

options.label: D
options.text: A blockchain ledger service for cryptocurrency transactions

explanation: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale relational databases in the cloud, automating time-consuming administrative tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, patching, and backups.

questionText: Which relational database engines are supported by Amazon RDS? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: PostgreSQL

options.label: B
options.text: MySQL

options.label: C
options.text: Apache Cassandra

options.label: D
options.text: MongoDB

options.label: E
options.text: Redis

explanation: Amazon RDS natively supports six commercial and open-source database engines: Amazon Aurora, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server.

questionText: What is Amazon Aurora?

options.label: A
options.text: An AWS-built MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database engine built for the cloud that offers up to 5x the throughput of standard MySQL

options.label: B
options.text: A cold object storage tier for photos

options.label: C
options.text: A real-time text-to-speech AI engine

options.label: D
options.text: A virtual private network gateway for branch offices

explanation: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational database engine designed for the cloud that is fully compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. It delivers up to 5x the throughput of standard MySQL and 3x the throughput of standard PostgreSQL.

questionText: How does Amazon Aurora achieve high durability and fault tolerance for stored database data?

options.label: A
options.text: By maintaining 6 copies of data across 3 Availability Zones automatically

options.label: B
options.text: By storing a single copy on a magnetic tape in Virginia

options.label: C
options.text: By asking the customer to run manual export scripts daily

options.label: D
options.text: By relying on local instance store volumes exclusively

explanation: Amazon Aurora storage is distributed across a fleet of storage nodes, maintaining six copies of your data across three Availability Zones. It continuously backs up your data to Amazon S3 with 99.999999999% durability.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment?

options.label: A
options.text: High availability and automatic failover in the event of hardware or AZ disruption

options.label: B
options.text: Scaling read performance for global analytical queries

options.label: C
options.text: Reducing monthly database billing costs by 50%

options.label: D
options.text: Providing a public IP address for external web developers

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ deployments synchronously replicate data to a standby database instance in a different Availability Zone. In the event of an infrastructure failure or maintenance, RDS automatically fails over to the standby instance with zero administrative intervention.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of an Amazon RDS Read Replica?

options.label: A
options.text: Scaling read-heavy database workloads horizontally and offloading reporting queries from the primary database

options.label: B
options.text: Providing synchronous automated disaster failover

options.label: C
options.text: Encrypting database backups with customer managed keys

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing storage volume size automatically

explanation: RDS Read Replicas asynchronously replicate data from the primary DB instance to scale read throughput horizontally for read-heavy database workloads and reporting queries, freeing up the primary instance for write operations.

questionText: What type of database is Amazon DynamoDB?

options.label: A
options.text: A fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database service

options.label: B
options.text: A relational database supporting standard SQL joins and stored procedures

options.label: C
options.text: A columnar data warehouse for enterprise business intelligence

options.label: D
options.text: A flat text file hosted on an S3 static web bucket

explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database service that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, with built-in security, backup and restore, and in-memory caching.

questionText: Which Amazon DynamoDB feature provides a fully managed, in-memory cache that reduces read response times from milliseconds to microseconds?

options.label: A
options.text: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon ElastiCache

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Aurora Replicas

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Glue Data Catalog

explanation: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to a 10x performance improvement—from milliseconds to microseconds—even at millions of requests per second.

questionText: Which AWS service is an in-memory data store and cache service supporting Redis and Memcached engines for fast sub-millisecond retrieval of session data?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon ElastiCache

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Redshift

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Neptune

options.label: D
options.text: AWS DataSync

explanation: Amazon ElastiCache is a fully managed in-memory data store and caching service compatible with Redis and Memcached engines, enabling applications to retrieve frequently accessed data with sub-millisecond latency.

questionText: What is Amazon Redshift?

options.label: A
options.text: A fast, fully managed, petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse service optimized for complex analytical queries (OLAP)

options.label: B
options.text: An in-memory key-value database for real-time mobile chat

options.label: C
options.text: A lightweight relational database for basic WordPress blogs

options.label: D
options.text: A message queuing service for microservices

explanation: Amazon Redshift is a fast, scalable, fully managed cloud data warehouse that makes it simple and cost-effective to analyze all your data across your data warehouse and data lake using standard SQL and business intelligence tools.

questionText: Which AWS service helps migrate relational databases, non-relational databases, and data warehouses to AWS with minimal application downtime?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS)

options.label: C
options.text: AWS DataSync

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Snowball Edge

explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) helps migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely. The source database remains fully operational during the migration, minimizing downtime to applications that rely on the database.

questionText: When migrating from an on-premises Oracle database to an open-source PostgreSQL database on Amazon Aurora, which tool helps convert the database schema and stored procedures?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Systems Manager Run Command

options.label: C
options.text: AWS CloudFormation

options.label: D
options.text: AWS X-Ray

explanation: The AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) makes heterogeneous database migrations predictable by automatically converting the source database schema and a majority of the database code (views, stored procedures, and functions) to the target database format.

questionText: Which AWS fully managed database service is optimized for storing and navigating highly connected data sets, such as social graphs, fraud detection networks, and knowledge graphs?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Neptune

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon DocumentDB

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Timestream

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon RDS for SQL Server

explanation: Amazon Neptune is a fast, reliable, fully managed graph database service that makes it easy to build and run applications that work with highly connected datasets, supporting popular graph query models like Apache TinkerPop Gremlin and SPARQL.

questionText: Which AWS managed database service is compatible with MongoDB workloads, allowing developers to store, query, and index JSON document data?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Redshift

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (QLDB)

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Keyspaces

explanation: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a scalable, highly durable, and fully managed document database service designed for storing, querying, and indexing JSON data with Apache 2.0 open-source MongoDB API compatibility.

questionText: Which AWS managed database service provides an immutable, cryptographically verifiable transaction log owned by a central trusted authority?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon DynamoDB

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Managed Blockchain

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Aurora Serverless

explanation: Amazon QLDB is a fully managed ledger database that provides a transparent, immutable, and cryptographically verifiable transaction log owned by a central trusted authority, ideal for tracking financial transactions and audit trails.

questionText: Which AWS database service is purpose-built for collecting, storing, and processing time-series data such as IoT sensor metrics and industrial telemetry at scale?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Timestream

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon RDS

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon SimpleDB

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Keyspaces

explanation: Amazon Timestream is a fast, scalable, and serverless time series database service for IoT and operational applications that makes it easy to store and analyze trillions of events per day up to 1,000 times faster and at 1/10th the cost of relational databases.

questionText: Which AWS database service is a managed, scalable, and serverless Apache Cassandra-compatible database service?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Redshift Spectrum

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon DynamoDB Streams

explanation: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is a scalable, highly available, and managed Apache Cassandra-compatible database service. You can run Cassandra workloads on AWS using the same Cassandra application code and developer tools.

questionText: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for Amazon RDS, which task is the responsibility of AWS? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Applying operating system patches to the database server host

options.label: B
options.text: Performing underlying hardware maintenance and power management

options.label: C
options.text: Designing database tables and defining relational foreign key constraints

options.label: D
options.text: Authoring optimized SQL SELECT and INSERT queries

options.label: E
options.text: Managing application user authentication passwords inside the database

explanation: Under the Shared Responsibility Model for RDS, AWS manages the underlying hardware, power, facility, physical infrastructure, operating system installation, and OS/DB engine security patching. The customer is responsible for schema design, queries, and data.

questionText: What happens during an automated failover of an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment?

options.label: A
options.text: RDS flips the canonical DNS name record of the DB instance to point to the standby DB instance in the secondary AZ

options.label: B
options.text: The application must change its database connection string IP address in code manually

options.label: C
options.text: All database tables are dropped and rebuilt from S3 backup archives

options.label: D
options.text: The primary instance is moved to an on-premises data center

explanation: During failover, Amazon RDS automatically flips the canonical DNS name record (CNAME) of the DB instance to point to the standby DB instance in the secondary AZ, allowing the application to reconnect without code modifications.

questionText: What is Amazon Aurora Serverless?

options.label: A
options.text: An on-demand, autoscaling configuration for Amazon Aurora where the database automatically starts up, scales compute capacity up or down based on application demand, and shuts down when idle

options.label: B
options.text: A database that does not store any data

options.label: C
options.text: A database that only runs on customer mobile devices

options.label: D
options.text: A free version of MySQL that has no security encryption

explanation: Amazon Aurora Serverless is an on-demand, autoscaling configuration for Amazon Aurora. It automatically starts up, shuts down, and scales capacity up or down based on your application's needs, billing only for database capacity consumed.

questionText: Which Amazon DynamoDB feature allows you to replicate tables automatically across multiple AWS Regions for global high availability and local low-latency reads?

options.label: A
options.text: DynamoDB Global Tables

options.label: B
options.text: DynamoDB Streams

options.label: C
options.text: DynamoDB Local

options.label: D
options.text: DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables builds upon DynamoDB's global footprint to provide fully managed, multi-Region, and multi-active replication, delivering fast local read and write performance for massive global applications.

questionText: What is Amazon DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)?

options.label: A
options.text: Continuous automatic backups that allow you to restore table data to any single second in the past 35 days

options.label: B
options.text: A tool that restores code commits from Git history

options.label: C
options.text: A billing refund feature for unused capacity

options.label: D
options.text: A snapshot tool that only runs on New Year's Day

explanation: Point-in-time recovery (PITR) provides continuous backups of your DynamoDB table data. When enabled, you can restore that table to any point in time from the past 35 days down to the exact second.

questionText: A business intelligence team needs to run complex aggregation queries across petabytes of historical sales data once a week. Which database engine is purpose-built for this workload?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Redshift

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon DynamoDB

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon RDS for MariaDB with micro instance

explanation: Amazon Redshift is a columnar OLAP data warehouse engineered for complex analytical aggregations across huge datasets (terabytes to petabytes), whereas OLTP engines like RDS or DynamoDB are designed for row-based transactional operations.

questionText: Which AWS service is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL without needing to load the data into a database?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Athena

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Redshift

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Aurora

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon DocumentDB

explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that makes it simple to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. You pay only for the queries that you run (per TB of data scanned).

questionText: What is the primary benefit of columnar data storage used by Amazon Redshift compared to traditional row-oriented storage used by Amazon RDS?

options.label: A
options.text: Columnar storage drastically reduces disk I/O requirements by reading only the specific columns referenced in an analytical SQL query

options.label: B
options.text: Columnar storage eliminates the need for primary keys in web shopping carts

options.label: C
options.text: Columnar storage allows data to be edited directly in Microsoft Word

options.label: D
options.text: Columnar storage prevents data from being stored on hard drives

explanation: Columnar storage organizes data on disk by columns rather than rows. For analytical queries that calculate aggregates (e.g., SUM or AVG) across a few columns over millions of rows, columnar storage only reads relevant columns, drastically reducing I/O.

questionText: What is Amazon CloudWatch?

options.label: A
options.text: A monitoring and management service that collects operational metrics, logs, and alarms from AWS resources and applications

options.label: B
options.text: A physical digital wristwatch shipped to AWS developers

options.label: C
options.text: A security camera streaming service for smart homes

options.label: D
options.text: A video conferencing client for team standups

explanation: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service that provides data and actionable insights for AWS, hybrid, and on-premises applications and infrastructure resources through metrics, logs, and automated alarms.

questionText: What is AWS CloudTrail?

options.label: A
options.text: A governance and auditing service that records account activity and API calls made across your AWS infrastructure

options.label: B
options.text: A guided nature walking tour organized by Amazon

options.label: C
options.text: A network routing protocol replacing BGP

options.label: D
options.text: A billing forecast spreadsheet tool

explanation: AWS CloudTrail records AWS account activity and tracks API calls made via the Management Console, AWS SDKs, and command-line tools. It provides event history of actions taken (who did what, when, and from where).

questionText: What is the key difference between Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail?

options.label: A
options.text: CloudWatch focuses on resource performance metrics and application logs; CloudTrail focuses on API call auditing and user activity tracking

options.label: B
options.text: CloudWatch is only used for billing, while CloudTrail is only used for databases

options.label: C
options.text: CloudWatch records video of users, while CloudTrail is a text chat tool

options.label: D
options.text: There is no difference between the two services

explanation: Amazon CloudWatch monitors resource performance, system health, operational metrics (CPU, disk, network), and application logs. AWS CloudTrail audits management and API activity, recording who made API calls, from which IP, and at what time.

questionText: An engineer needs to receive an SMS or email notification whenever an EC2 instance's CPU utilization exceeds 85% for five consecutive minutes. Which combination of services achieves this?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Alarm and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CloudTrail and AWS Artifact

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Direct Connect and Amazon S3 Glacier

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager and AWS Snowcone

explanation: You configure a CloudWatch Alarm to evaluate the CPUUtilization metric against an 85% threshold over a 5-minute period. When the alarm transitions to ALARM state, it publishes a notification to an Amazon SNS topic, sending an email or SMS.

questionText: What is AWS Config?

options.label: A
options.text: A service that enables you to assess, audit, and evaluate the configurations of your AWS resources and monitor compliance against rules

options.label: B
options.text: A text editor for writing Python scripts

options.label: C
options.text: A service for ordering server hardware from third parties

options.label: D
options.text: An automated code compiler for C++

explanation: AWS Config continuously monitors and records your AWS resource configurations and allows you to automate the evaluation of recorded configurations against desired configurations and compliance rules.

questionText: An auditor needs to verify whether all Amazon S3 buckets in an AWS account have server-side encryption enabled at all times. Which AWS service can continuously evaluate this compliance rule?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Config

options.label: B
options.text: AWS X-Ray

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Route 53

explanation: AWS Config provides managed rules (such as s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled) that continuously evaluate the configuration settings of AWS resources and flag non-compliant resources in real time.

questionText: What is AWS CloudFormation?

options.label: A
options.text: An Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service that lets you model, provision, and manage AWS and third-party resources using JSON or YAML templates

options.label: B
options.text: A meteorological storm warning service

options.label: C
options.text: A drag-and-drop website design builder

options.label: D
options.text: A tool for configuring home broadband routers

explanation: AWS CloudFormation allows you to treat Infrastructure as Code (IaC). You describe all your desired AWS resources (EC2, VPC, S3) in a declarative JSON or YAML template, and CloudFormation provisions and configures them reliably and repeatably.

questionText: What is a CloudFormation Stack?

options.label: A
options.text: A collection of AWS resources that you can manage as a single unified unit, created, updated, or deleted via a CloudFormation template

options.label: B
options.text: A physical stack of server blades in a server rack

options.label: C
options.text: A list of customer credit card transactions

options.label: D
options.text: A memory buffer inside the CPU

explanation: A CloudFormation Stack is a collection of AWS resources that you manage as a single unit. You can create, update, or delete a collection of resources by creating, updating, or deleting stacks using CloudFormation templates.

questionText: What is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?

options.label: A
options.text: A Platform as a Service (PaaS) that makes it easy to deploy, run, and scale web applications and services without configuring underlying infrastructure

options.label: B
options.text: A serverless distributed database engine

options.label: C
options.text: An agricultural forecasting software tool

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware network switch installed in corporate data centers

explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an easy-to-use Platform as a Service (PaaS) for deploying and scaling web applications and services developed with Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and Docker on familiar servers like Apache and Nginx.

questionText: How does AWS Elastic Beanstalk differ from AWS CloudFormation?

options.label: A
options.text: Beanstalk focuses specifically on deploying application code (PaaS) with automated environment provisioning; CloudFormation provides low-level Infrastructure as Code control across virtually all AWS resources

options.label: B
options.text: Beanstalk requires writing JSON templates; CloudFormation is only managed via phone calls

options.label: C
options.text: CloudFormation cannot create EC2 instances

options.label: D
options.text: Beanstalk is only for offline mobile apps

explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform as a Service designed for web developers to deploy code without worrying about infrastructure provisioning. CloudFormation is an Infrastructure as Code engine providing granular control over all AWS resource definitions.

questionText: What is AWS Systems Manager (SSM)?

options.label: A
options.text: A centralized operations hub for visibility and control of your AWS resources, automating operational tasks and patch management across cloud and on-premises servers

options.label: B
options.text: A human resources portal for hiring Amazon employees

options.label: C
options.text: A computer motherboard firmware update tool

options.label: D
options.text: A physical inventory barcode scanner

explanation: AWS Systems Manager gives you visibility and control of your infrastructure on AWS. It provides a unified user interface so you can view operational data from multiple AWS services and automate operational tasks across your resources.

questionText: Which capability of AWS Systems Manager allows administrators to securely manage EC2 instances through an interactive one-click browser-based shell or CLI without opening inbound SSH ports or managing bastion hosts?

options.label: A
options.text: Session Manager

options.label: B
options.text: Run Command

options.label: C
options.text: Patch Manager

options.label: D
options.text: Inventory

explanation: Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure and auditable instance management without needing to open inbound ports, maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys. Connections are routed over HTTPS via the SSM Agent.

questionText: Which capability of AWS Systems Manager provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and secrets management (such as database passwords and API keys)?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) console

options.label: C
options.text: AWS CloudTrail insights

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault

explanation: Systems Manager Parameter Store provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and secrets management. You can store data such as passwords, database strings, and license codes as plain text or encrypted data.

questionText: What is AWS X-Ray?

options.label: A
options.text: A service that helps developers analyze and debug distributed applications, such as those built using a microservices architecture

options.label: B
options.text: A medical imaging archive for radiological DICOM scans

options.label: C
options.text: A physical scanner for baggage at AWS data centers

options.label: D
options.text: A network penetration testing tool

explanation: AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug production, distributed applications, such as those built using a microservices architecture. It generates end-to-end service maps showing request paths and latency bottlenecks.

questionText: What is the AWS Health Dashboard (Personal Health Dashboard)?

options.label: A
options.text: A dashboard that provides personalized alerts and guidance when AWS is experiencing events that may affect your specific account resources

options.label: B
options.text: A wearable fitness monitor integration service

options.label: C
options.text: An employee medical insurance claim portal

options.label: D
options.text: A global list showing whether general public websites are online

explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard (formerly Personal Health Dashboard) provides personalized information about events that can affect your specific AWS account and resources, alerting you to performance disruptions or scheduled maintenance.

questionText: How does the AWS Health Dashboard differ from the general AWS Service Health Dashboard?

options.label: A
options.text: The Service Health Dashboard displays the general status of AWS services globally; the Personal Health Dashboard displays events that specifically impact your account's provisioned resources

options.label: B
options.text: The Personal Health Dashboard costs $10,000/month; the Service Health Dashboard is free

options.label: C
options.text: The Service Health Dashboard requires an Enterprise Support plan

options.label: D
options.text: There is no difference between them

explanation: The AWS Service Health Dashboard displays the general operational status of all AWS services across all public Regions worldwide. The AWS Health Dashboard (Personal) gives proactive, targeted notifications tailored to your specific account resources.

questionText: What is AWS OpsWorks?

options.label: A
options.text: A configuration management service that provides managed instances of Chef and Puppet to automate server configuration using code

options.label: B
options.text: An enterprise email and calendar server

options.label: C
options.text: A desktop publishing application

options.label: D
options.text: A video rendering pipeline for Hollywood films

explanation: AWS OpsWorks is a configuration management service that helps you use Chef and Puppet to configure and operate applications in your cloud enterprise, automating server deployment, patching, and configuration management.

questionText: Which AWS service allows you to define application infrastructure in familiar programming languages such as TypeScript, Python, Java, and C#, generating CloudFormation templates automatically?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM)

options.label: C
options.text: AWS CodeStar

options.label: D
options.text: AWS App Mesh

explanation: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework to define cloud application resources using familiar programming languages (TypeScript, Python, Java, C#), synthesizing them into CloudFormation.

questionText: What is CloudWatch Logs Insights?

options.label: A
options.text: An interactive query engine that allows you to search and analyze log data stored in Amazon CloudWatch Logs using a purpose-built query language

options.label: B
options.text: A service that posts system logs to public social media accounts

options.label: C
options.text: A tool that converts system logs into audio podcasts

options.label: D
options.text: An encryption service for physical tape drives

explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights enables you to interactively search and analyze your log data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. You can perform queries with aggregations, filters, and regular expressions to quickly troubleshoot operational issues.

questionText: What type of CloudWatch metric is NOT collected by default from Amazon EC2 instances unless a CloudWatch agent is installed inside the operating system?

options.label: A
options.text: Memory (RAM) utilization and available disk space

options.label: B
options.text: CPU utilization

options.label: C
options.text: Network bytes in and network bytes out

options.label: D
options.text: Disk read/write bytes for instance hypervisor metrics

explanation: Hypervisor-level metrics like CPU utilization, network traffic, and disk I/O are tracked by default. Internal OS metrics such as memory (RAM) consumption and disk space utilization require the CloudWatch unified agent inside the guest OS.

questionText: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)?

options.label: A
options.text: A fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications

options.label: B
options.text: A real-time live video streaming server

options.label: C
options.text: A database engine for storing employee phone numbers

options.label: D
options.text: A physical printer spooler for AWS offices

explanation: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Messages are stored reliably until processed and deleted by consumer applications.

questionText: What is the primary difference between SQS Standard queues and SQS FIFO queues?

options.label: A
options.text: Standard queues offer nearly unlimited throughput with best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery; FIFO queues guarantee exact First-In-First-Out ordering and exactly-once processing

options.label: B
options.text: Standard queues cost $1,000 per message; FIFO queues are free

options.label: C
options.text: FIFO queues only support video files

options.label: D
options.text: Standard queues delete messages immediately after receipt without consumer processing

explanation: SQS Standard queues provide unlimited throughput, best-effort ordering, and at-least-once delivery. SQS FIFO (First-In, First-Out) queues guarantee that messages are delivered exactly once and processed in the exact order that they are sent.

questionText: What is the purpose of the Visibility Timeout in Amazon SQS?

options.label: A
options.text: The period of time during which SQS prevents other consumers from receiving and processing a message that has already been retrieved by one consumer

options.label: B
options.text: The time it takes for an administrator's screen to turn off due to inactivity

options.label: C
options.text: The duration an S3 object remains public on the web

options.label: D
options.text: The timeout before an EC2 instance is terminated during billing audits

explanation: When a consumer receives a message from an SQS queue, the message remains in the queue while the consumer processes it. The Visibility Timeout prevents other consumers from seeing and processing the same message concurrently.

questionText: What is an SQS Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)?

options.label: A
options.text: A designated queue to which messages are automatically moved if consumer applications fail to process them successfully after a maximum number of attempts

options.label: B
options.text: A queue that stores unroutable postal letters sent to Amazon headquarters

options.label: C
options.text: A queue used exclusively for deleted user accounts

options.label: D
options.text: An archived queue stored in cold tape storage

explanation: A Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) is a queue that other source queues can target to isolate messages that cannot be processed successfully (poison pill messages) after a designated maximum number of receive attempts.

questionText: What is Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)?

options.label: A
options.text: A fully managed pub/sub messaging and notification service for both application-to-application (A2A) and application-to-person (A2P) communication

options.label: B
options.text: A desktop push notification blocker for web browsers

options.label: C
options.text: A hardware bell installed in corporate security rooms

options.label: D
options.text: A social networking mobile app

explanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub service. Publishers send messages to topics, and subscribers (such as AWS Lambda, Amazon SQS, HTTP endpoints, mobile SMS, email) receive notifications instantly.

questionText: How does Amazon SQS differ from Amazon SNS in terms of message delivery communication patterns?

options.label: A
options.text: SQS uses a pull-based (polling) message queue model; SNS uses a push-based publisher/subscriber fan-out model

options.label: B
options.text: SQS sends messages to mobile phones; SNS is strictly an on-premises database

options.label: C
options.text: SNS requires consumers to continually poll for new messages

options.label: D
options.text: There is no architectural difference between them

explanation: SQS uses a pull model where consumers actively poll the queue to retrieve and delete messages. SNS uses a push model where messages published to a topic are immediately fanned out and pushed to all registered subscribers.

questionText: What is the SNS Fanout architectural pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: A message published to an SNS topic is replicated and pushed to multiple subscribed Amazon SQS queues for parallel, asynchronous processing by independent microservices

options.label: B
options.text: Spreading hardware cooling fans across multiple server racks

options.label: C
options.text: Distributing customer support tickets to overseas call centers

options.label: D
options.text: Broadcasting unencrypted passwords to all IAM users

explanation: The Fanout pattern occurs when a message published to an SNS topic is immediately distributed to multiple SQS queues in parallel. This enables decoupled microservices to perform different processing tasks simultaneously on the same message.

questionText: What is Amazon EventBridge?

options.label: A
options.text: A serverless event bus service that makes it easy to connect applications using data from your own applications, integrated SaaS applications, and AWS services

options.label: B
options.text: A physical suspension bridge constructed near Amazon facilities

options.label: C
options.text: A software protocol for connecting Bluetooth speakers

options.label: D
options.text: A calendar scheduling assistant for executive meetings

explanation: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that ingests data from your applications, third-party SaaS partners (like Datadog, Zendesk, Salesforce), and AWS services, routing events to targets based on declarative rules.

questionText: Which AWS service is an open-source compatible managed message broker for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, helping companies migrate legacy message queues without rewriting application code?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon MQ

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon SQS

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Kinesis

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon SimpleDB

explanation: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ. It makes it easy to migrate message brokers to the cloud without rewriting your messaging code by supporting industry-standard protocols (JMS, NMS, AMQP, STOMP, MQTT).

questionText: What is Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)?

options.label: A
options.text: A cost-effective, flexible, and scalable email service that enables developers to send transactional, marketing, or mass email communications

options.label: B
options.text: An internal corporate webmail client replacing Microsoft Outlook

options.label: C
options.text: An email spam filter deployed on physical office servers

options.label: D
options.text: A paper postal mailing service managed by Amazon

explanation: Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) is an email platform that provides an easy, cost-effective way for you to send and receive email using your own email addresses and domains for transactional and marketing messages.

questionText: What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?

options.label: A
options.text: A massively scalable and durable real-time data streaming service that can capture gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources

options.label: B
options.text: A water cooling monitoring system in data centers

options.label: C
options.text: A file compression format used for S3 archives

options.label: D
options.text: A desktop tool for converting audio files

explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is a scalable real-time streaming service that continuously captures gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources (such as financial transactions, IoT telemetry, social media feeds, and clickstreams).

questionText: Which member of the Amazon Kinesis family easily captures, transforms, and automatically loads streaming data into Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and OpenSearch with minimal configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Glue DataBrew

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon SQS FIFO

explanation: Amazon Data Firehose is the easiest way to reliably load streaming data into data lakes, warehouses, and analytics services. It captures, transforms, and loads streaming data into Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and OpenSearch automatically.

questionText: What is AWS AppSync?

options.label: A
options.text: A fully managed enterprise GraphQL and Pub/Sub API service that simplifies application development by connecting applications to data and events

options.label: B
options.text: A file synchronization client for syncing desktop folders with S3

options.label: C
options.text: An automatic smartphone battery charging station

options.label: D
options.text: A tool for merging Git branches across accounts

explanation: AWS AppSync is a fully managed service that makes it easy to develop GraphQL and real-time Pub/Sub APIs that connect applications to data sources (such as Amazon DynamoDB, AWS Lambda, and HTTP APIs).

questionText: What is Amazon API Gateway?

options.label: A
options.text: A fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure RESTful and WebSocket APIs at any scale

options.label: B
options.text: A physical gateway turnstile in an office reception area

options.label: C
options.text: A domain name registrar for registering .com domains

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware firewall appliance for home internet connections

explanation: Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale. It acts as the 'front door' for applications to access data, business logic, or backend services.

questionText: How does Amazon SQS Long Polling reduce application costs compared to Short Polling?

options.label: A
options.text: Long polling allows the SQS service to wait up to 20 seconds for a message to arrive in the queue before sending an empty response, eliminating empty responses and reducing API call charges

options.label: B
options.text: Long polling compresses message sizes by 99%

options.label: C
options.text: Long polling allows messages to be sent for free on weekends

options.label: D
options.text: Long polling deletes all messages without reading them

explanation: Long polling helps reduce the cost of using SQS by eliminating empty responses when there are no messages available and reducing false empty responses. It allows the receive call to wait up to 20 seconds for messages to arrive.

questionText: Which AWS service is designed for business-to-consumer (B2C) communication, allowing marketers and developers to engage customers across channels like email, SMS, push notifications, and voice?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Pinpoint

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Shield

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

explanation: Amazon Pinpoint is a multichannel marketing communication service that you can use to send targeted, personalized messages to customers over channels like email, SMS, mobile push, and in-app messaging.

questionText: What is the primary benefit of loose coupling in distributed cloud architectures achieved through messaging services like SQS and SNS?

options.label: A
options.text: Components function independently so that a failure or latency spike in one component does not cascade and crash the entire system

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees that software code never requires testing

options.label: C
options.text: It eliminates all software licensing fees completely

options.label: D
options.text: It forces all servers to run the identical operating system version

explanation: Loose coupling ensures that components of a system have minimal dependencies on each other. If one component fails or slows down, messages buffer safely in queues, preventing cascading system-wide crashes.

questionText: What are the three distinct types of offers available under the AWS Free Tier?

options.label: A
options.text: Always Free, 12 Months Free, and Short-Term Trials

options.label: B
options.text: Bronze, Silver, and Gold Free

options.label: C
options.text: Developer, Business, and Enterprise Free

options.label: D
options.text: Public, Private, and Hybrid Free

explanation: The AWS Free Tier consists of three distinct types of offers: 1) Always Free (offers that do not expire, such as DynamoDB 25 GB, Lambda 1M requests), 2) 12 Months Free (available for 12 months following initial signup, e.g., 750 hours/month of t2/t3.micro EC2), and 3) Short-Term Trials (trial periods activated upon service enablement).

questionText: Which AWS service is an example of an 'Always Free' offer in the AWS Free Tier?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Lambda (first 1 million requests per month free)

options.label: B
options.text: Amazon EC2 m5.large instances

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Redshift petabyte clusters

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Direct Connect 10 Gbps dedicated circuits

explanation: AWS Lambda includes 1 million free requests and 3.2 million seconds of compute time per month as an 'Always Free' tier offer that does not expire after 12 months.

questionText: What is a core characteristic of the '12 Months Free' tier offer for new AWS accounts?

options.label: A
options.text: It begins the day you sign up for an AWS account and expires exactly 12 months later

options.label: B
options.text: It automatically renews every calendar year for life

options.label: C
options.text: It requires signing an upfront 3-year non-disclosure contract

options.label: D
options.text: It is only available to educational universities

explanation: 12 Months Free tier benefits (such as 750 hours/month of EC2 Linux/Windows t2.micro or t3.micro instances and 5 GB of S3 standard storage) are valid for exactly 12 months starting from initial AWS account creation.

questionText: What is the primary pricing model of AWS cloud computing?

options.label: A
options.text: Pay-as-you-go (pay only for the individual services you consume without long-term contracts)

options.label: B
options.text: Flat mandatory $500 monthly membership subscription

options.label: C
options.text: Fixed 5-year hardware lease agreements

options.label: D
options.text: Per-employee payroll tax calculation

explanation: AWS provides a pay-as-you-go approach for pricing for over 200 cloud services. With AWS you pay only for the individual services you need, for as long as you use them, and without requiring long-term contracts or complex licensing.

questionText: Which fundamental pricing principle of AWS allows customers to lower costs as their data storage or service consumption grows?

options.label: A
options.text: Pay less by using more (tiered volume discounts)

options.label: B
options.text: Pay more to get faster customer support responses

options.label: C
options.text: Pay flat rate regardless of scale

options.label: D
options.text: Pay upfront penalties for high bandwidth

explanation: 'Pay less by using more' means AWS provides tiered volume discounts. For services like Amazon S3, storage pricing per gigabyte decreases as your total stored volume reaches higher tiers (e.g., first 50 TB, next 450 TB, over 500 TB).

questionText: Which direction of network data transfer is typically FREE of charge across virtually all AWS services?

options.label: A
options.text: Inbound data transfer from the Internet into AWS

options.label: B
options.text: Outbound data transfer from AWS to the Internet

options.label: C
options.text: Inter-region data transfer across oceans

options.label: D
options.text: Data transfer out to on-premises networks over VPN

explanation: Inbound data transfer from the Internet into AWS resources is completely free across all AWS services. AWS charges for outbound data transfer to the Internet (Data Transfer OUT) after the initial 100 GB/month free tier allowance.

questionText: Which network data transfer scenario incurs data transfer charges? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Transferring data outbound from an Amazon EC2 instance to the public Internet

options.label: B
options.text: Transferring data between two EC2 instances located in different AWS Regions

options.label: C
options.text: Uploading files from a corporate laptop into an Amazon S3 bucket (inbound)

options.label: D
options.text: Transferring data between an EC2 instance and an S3 bucket within the exact same AWS Region

options.label: E
options.text: Inbound network traffic arriving through an Internet Gateway

explanation: Data transfer outbound to the Internet and inter-region data transfer (moving data between two different AWS Regions) incur standard data egress fees. Inbound traffic and same-region S3 transfers are free.

questionText: Which tool should an architect use to model and estimate the expected monthly cost of a proposed multi-tier AWS architecture before creating any resources?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Pricing Calculator

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Cost Explorer

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Budgets

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator is a web-based planning tool that allows you to create cost estimates for your proposed architecture use cases on AWS before deploying any resources, with shareable summary links.

questionText: What was the previous name of the AWS tool replaced by the AWS Pricing Calculator?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Simple Monthly Calculator

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Billing Manager

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Cost Matrix

explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator is the modern, interactive replacement for the retired AWS Simple Monthly Calculator, providing granular estimates for newer AWS instance types and services.

questionText: Which pricing principle rewards customers who commit to consistent compute usage (e.g., measured in $/hour) for a 1-year or 3-year period?

options.label: A
options.text: Save when you commit (Savings Plans and Reserved Instances)

options.label: B
options.text: Pay-as-you-go On-Demand

options.label: C
options.text: Always Free tier

options.label: D
options.text: Dynamic Spot bidding

explanation: 'Save when you commit' allows customers to achieve savings of up to 72% over On-Demand rates by committing to a consistent amount of compute usage (e.g., $10/hour) for a 1-year or 3-year term via Savings Plans or Reserved Instances.

questionText: How does AWS achieve economies of scale that enable frequent price reductions for customers?

options.label: A
options.text: As hundreds of thousands of customers use AWS, AWS can procure hardware at massive scale and pass the resulting cost savings back to customers as lower prices

options.label: B
options.text: By charging customers hidden monthly maintenance fees

options.label: C
options.text: By reducing the durability of stored customer data

options.label: D
options.text: By eliminating 24/7 technical customer support

explanation: As AWS grows, the scale of infrastructure and operations creates massive economies of scale. AWS continuously optimizes operational efficiencies and passes those savings back to customers in the form of lower pricing.

questionText: Under the AWS Free Tier, how many hours per month of Amazon EC2 t2.micro (or t3.micro in regions where t2 is unavailable) are included for the first 12 months?

options.label: A
options.text: 750 hours per month (enough to run one instance continuously 24/7)

options.label: B
options.text: 100 hours per month

options.label: C
options.text: 50 hours per month

options.label: D
options.text: 24 hours per month

explanation: The AWS Free Tier includes 750 hours of Linux and 750 hours of Windows t2.micro/t3.micro instances each month for 12 months, which is sufficient to keep a single instance running continuously all month.

questionText: Which storage amount is provided free per month for the first 12 months under the AWS Free Tier for Amazon S3 Standard?

options.label: A
options.text: 5 GB of standard storage, 20,000 GET requests, and 2,000 PUT requests

options.label: B
options.text: 100 GB of standard storage

options.label: C
options.text: 1 TB of standard storage

options.label: D
options.text: 500 MB of standard storage

explanation: The S3 Free Tier offer includes 5 GB of Amazon S3 standard storage, 20,000 GET requests, and 2,000 PUT requests per month for 12 months following initial AWS account registration.

questionText: What is a 'Short-Term Trial' in the AWS Free Tier?

options.label: A
options.text: A free trial that activates when a specific service is first used, lasting for a defined period or until a usage quota is met

options.label: B
options.text: A 1-hour phone consultation with an AWS sales executive

options.label: C
options.text: A trial that requires paying a non-refundable deposit

options.label: D
options.text: A trial only available during Amazon Prime Day

explanation: Short-Term Trials are free trial offers that activate on the day you first start using a specific service (e.g., 30 days of Amazon Inspector or Amazon GuardDuty free), regardless of when your AWS account was originally created.

questionText: What happens if a customer exceeds the free usage tier limits within a given month?

options.label: A
options.text: Standard pay-as-you-go On-Demand service rates apply to any usage exceeding the free tier allowance

options.label: B
options.text: The entire AWS account is suspended and all instances are terminated

options.label: C
options.text: AWS issues a warning fine of $500

options.label: D
options.text: The account is permanently converted to an Enterprise Support agreement

explanation: If your resource usage exceeds the monthly Free Tier limits, your account is simply charged standard pay-as-you-go service rates for the additional usage beyond the free tier limits.

questionText: Does Amazon RDS include free tier hours during the first 12 months of account registration?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, 750 hours per month of db.t2.micro/db.t3.micro/db.t4g.micro Single-AZ instance usage with 20 GB of general purpose SSD storage

questionText: Which AWS pricing concept describes a customer paying an upfront amount to lock in lower hourly rates on Reserved Instances?

questionText: Why is data transfer between two Amazon EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same Region billed, while data transfer in the same AZ using private IPs is free?

options.label: A
options.text: Traffic between AZs traverses the redundant inter-AZ optical metro backbone, incurring modest inter-AZ networking charges ($0.01/GB each direction)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS penalizes multi-AZ architecture to encourage single AZ deployments

options.text: Inter-AZ traffic requires satellite communication links

options.label: D

questionText: What is AWS Cost Explorer?

options.label: A
options.text: A tool that enables you to visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time, including forecasting future spend up to 12 months

options.label: B
options.text: An IDE plugin for debugging Java applications

options.label: C
options.text: A security vulnerability assessment scanner

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware barcode reader for warehouse assets

explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an easy-to-use interface that lets you visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time. It creates custom reports and forecasts spending up to 12 months into the future.

questionText: What is the primary function of AWS Budgets?

options.label: A
options.text: To set custom cost and usage limits that trigger automated email or SNS alerts when actual or forecasted spend exceeds your defined thresholds

options.label: B
options.text: To negotiate lower hardware prices directly with Amazon suppliers

options.label: C
options.text: To automatically liquidate underperforming company stock

options.label: D
options.text: To restrict employees from browsing social media during work hours

explanation: AWS Budgets allows you to track and set custom budgets for costs, usage, reservations, and Savings Plans. You receive alerts (via SNS or email) when actual or forecasted metrics exceed your threshold.

questionText: How does AWS Budgets differ from AWS Cost Explorer?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cost Explorer is designed for historical visualization and forecasting; AWS Budgets is designed for setting proactive alerts and automated actions when spending limits are reached

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Budgets is only for educational accounts; Cost Explorer is for commercial enterprises

options.label: C
options.text: Cost Explorer cannot display past data; Budgets cannot send alerts

options.label: D
options.text: There is no difference between the two tools

explanation: Cost Explorer is an analytics tool used to visualize and analyze historical spending patterns and project future costs. AWS Budgets is a proactive governance tool used to define targets and trigger alerts when costs or usage exceed limits.

questionText: What is the most detailed and comprehensive source of AWS billing and usage data available, delivering raw CSV or Parquet files to an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Monthly Billing Summary PDF

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor Report

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Metrics Export

explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) is the single most comprehensive dataset of AWS cost and usage available. It lists usage for each service category used by an account and its IAM users in hourly or daily line items delivered to S3.

questionText: What are Cost Allocation Tags in AWS?

options.label: A
options.text: Key-value labels attached to AWS resources used to organize, track, and categorize resource costs on your AWS billing reports

options.label: B
options.text: Physical RFID security badges worn by datacenter employees

options.label: C
options.text: Discount coupons distributed via marketing newsletters

options.label: D
options.text: DNS records used to route internal microservices

explanation: Cost Allocation Tags are metadata key-value pairs (e.g., Environment: Production, CostCenter: 1042) that you attach to AWS resources. Once activated in the Billing console, AWS organizes cost data by tags on billing reports and Cost Explorer.

questionText: What are the two categories of Cost Allocation Tags available in AWS?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS-Generated Tags (e.g., aws:createdBy) and User-Defined Tags (e.g., Project: Alpha)

options.label: B
options.text: Public Tags and Private Tags

options.label: C
options.text: Hardware Tags and Software Tags

options.label: D
options.text: Encrypted Tags and Plaintext Tags

explanation: Cost Allocation Tags consist of: 1) AWS-Generated Tags (prefixed with 'aws:' such as aws:createdBy, automatically applied by AWS), and 2) User-Defined Tags (created and applied directly by users, e.g., CostCenter, Owner, Environment).

questionText: Before Cost Allocation Tags appear on AWS billing reports or in AWS Cost Explorer, what mandatory step must be taken by an administrator?

options.label: A
options.text: The tags must be explicitly activated in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console

options.label: B
options.text: The AWS account must be upgraded to Enterprise Support

options.label: C
options.text: All EC2 instances must be rebooted

options.label: D
options.text: A formal request ticket must be submitted to AWS Premium Support

explanation: Creating a tag on a resource does not automatically make it appear on billing statements. An administrator must explicitly activate the tag as a Cost Allocation Tag in the Billing and Cost Management console.

questionText: What is AWS Cost Anomaly Detection?

options.label: A
options.text: A machine learning service that continuously monitors cost and usage to identify anomalous spending and root causes automatically

options.label: B
options.text: A tool that detects corrupted hard drive sectors on EBS volumes

options.label: C
options.text: A security scanner that finds infected JavaScript files

options.label: D
options.text: A tool that spots counterfeit credit cards during signup

explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses advanced machine learning models to identify unexpected spending spikes and detect cost anomalies across your AWS accounts, identifying the root cause service and alerting administrators.

questionText: What is AWS Billing Conductor?

options.label: A
options.text: A customizable billing service that allows enterprises and AWS Solution Providers to customize, model, and allocate pro forma billing rates for internal business units or end customers

options.label: B
options.text: A musical orchestration tool built for Amazon Studios

options.label: C
options.text: A physical electrical cable routing device inside server chassis

options.label: D
options.text: A credit scoring tool used for corporate credit card applications

explanation: AWS Billing Conductor is a fully managed service that provides a customizable billing engine to model the billing relationship between you and your customers or internal business units, generating customized pro-forma invoices.

questionText: What action can AWS Budgets automatically trigger when a budget threshold is exceeded (AWS Budget Actions)?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply an IAM policy, attach a Service Control Policy, or stop specific EC2 or RDS instances

options.label: B
options.text: Delete the customer's AWS root account permanently

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically charge the customer's secondary credit card

options.label: D
options.text: Cancel the company's Internet service provider contract

explanation: AWS Budget Actions allow you to configure automated or semi-automated responses when a budget limit is breached, such as applying a restrictive IAM policy to prevent new resources, or stopping specific EC2 or RDS instances.

questionText: Which tool provides visual recommendations for purchasing Reserved Instances and Savings Plans based on past usage history?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cost Explorer recommendations

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CloudFormation designer

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon GuardDuty findings

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager Run Command

explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides personalized recommendations for purchasing Reserved Instances and Savings Plans by analyzing your historical compute usage over the past 30 or 60 days to calculate potential savings.

questionText: What is the minimum granularity at which AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) can break down usage data?

options.label: A
options.text: Hourly

options.label: B
options.text: Per-second

options.label: C
options.text: Monthly only

options.label: D
options.text: Yearly

explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports can be generated with either hourly or daily granularity, providing itemized breakdown of costs, usage quantities, resource IDs, and cost allocation tags.

questionText: A company wants to query its raw AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) stored in Amazon S3 using standard SQL syntax. Which combination of services provides this capability serverlessly?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Athena and Amazon S3

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Snowcone and Amazon DynamoDB

options.label: C
