options.label: D
options.text: AWS Systems Manager and AWS Artifact

explanation: By delivering the AWS Cost and Usage Report in Parquet format to an S3 bucket and integrating it with the AWS Glue Data Catalog, you can run serverless SQL queries against your detailed billing records using Amazon Athena.

questionText: Which metric can be tracked using AWS Budgets? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Cost budgets (tracking total dollar expenditures)

options.label: B
options.text: Usage budgets (tracking usage amounts for specific services like EC2 hours or S3 GB)

options.label: C
options.text: Room temperature in AWS server rooms

options.label: D
options.text: Typing speed of remote developers

options.label: E
options.text: Number of email spam messages received by employees

explanation: AWS Budgets supports: 1) Cost budgets (dollar spend), 2) Usage budgets (measure unit usage, e.g., gigabytes or instance hours), 3) RI utilization and coverage budgets, and 4) Savings Plans utilization and coverage budgets.

questionText: What is an AWS Credit in billing?

options.label: A
options.text: A promotional or service credit applied directly to an AWS account invoice to offset eligible service charges

options.label: B
options.text: A loan provided by Amazon Bank to purchase physical servers

options.label: C
options.text: A virtual cryptocurrency token traded on decentralized exchanges

options.label: D
options.text: A rating score assessing customer creditworthiness

explanation: AWS Credits are promotional codes or goodwill credits applied to your AWS account balance that automatically offset eligible AWS service charges on your monthly bill until the credit balance or expiration date is reached.

questionText: Which tool allows you to view your current estimated monthly billing charges directly on the AWS Management Console dashboard?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Billing and Cost Management Dashboard

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CodeCommit Console

options.label: C
options.text: Amazon Route 53 Dashboard

options.label: D
options.text: AWS Certificate Manager

explanation: The AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard gives a high-level summary of your current estimated charges, month-to-date spending, highest-spend services, and budget tracking widgets.

questionText: Can AWS Cost Explorer forecast costs for unreleased AWS services that your account has never deployed?

options.label: A
options.text: No, Cost Explorer forecasts future spend based solely on the account's historical usage data patterns

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, if an enterprise contract is signed

options.label: D
options.text: Only for Amazon S3 storage classes

explanation: AWS Cost Explorer's forecasting algorithm relies on historical spending and consumption models over past months. It cannot forecast costs for services or architectures that have zero historical usage data.

questionText: What is the maximum forecasting horizon available in AWS Cost Explorer?

options.label: A
options.text: Up to 12 months into the future

options.label: B
options.text: Up to 10 years

options.label: C
options.text: 7 days only

options.label: D
options.text: 30 days only

explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides cost and usage forecasts up to 12 months into the future based on past usage patterns and linear regression modeling.

questionText: How can a company receive an alert when their AWS bill is forecasted to exceed $5,000 by the end of the current month?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an AWS Budget with a forecasted spend threshold of $5,000 and configure an email notification

options.label: B
options.text: Call Amazon headquarters every morning on the telephone

options.label: C
options.text: Set up an IAM password expiration policy

options.label: D
options.text: Reboot all EC2 instances once weekly

explanation: AWS Budgets allows you to set an alert based on forecasted spend. If current consumption trends indicate that the monthly total will exceed the $5,000 threshold, AWS Budgets sends an alert before the overrun occurs.

questionText: Which AWS service provides an aggregated view of resource tags across multiple AWS services and AWS accounts?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Resource Groups & Tag Editor

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Shield Advanced

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Inspector

explanation: AWS Resource Groups and Tag Editor lets you search, view, and edit tags across hundreds of AWS resources simultaneously across multiple regions in your account.

questionText: Which AWS pricing model is best suited for an application that runs 24/7 with steady, unchanging compute requirements over a 3-year production lifecycle?

options.label: A
options.text: Compute Savings Plans or Standard Reserved Instances with 3-year commitment

options.label: B
options.text: On-Demand Instances with zero upfront payment

options.label: C
options.text: Spot Instances with dynamic bid prices

options.label: D
options.text: Short-term trial licenses

explanation: For continuous, steady-state baseline workloads with a 3-year timeline, a 3-year Savings Plan or Reserved Instance offers the maximum available cost discount (up to 72%) compared to paying On-Demand rates.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of AWS Purchase Order Management in the Billing console?

options.label: A
options.text: To configure and manage enterprise Purchase Orders (POs) and map them to AWS electronic billing invoices

options.text: To purchase office furniture from Amazon.com

options.text: To order promotional t-shirts for AWS conferences

questionText: How does AWS calculate charges for Amazon EBS gp3 volumes?

options.label: A
options.text: Based on provisioned storage capacity (GB-month), with baseline IOPS (3,000) and throughput (125 MB/s) included free, charging only for provisioned performance above those baselines

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: A flat fee of $10 per volume regardless of size

options.label: D
options.text: Only when instances are turned off

questionText: Which billing tool sends daily, weekly, or monthly automated budget email reports to designated stakeholders without requiring them to log in to the AWS console?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Budget Reports

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Route 53 Resolver

explanation: AWS Budget Reports allows you to create scheduled email reports that automatically deliver the status of your existing budgets to corporate stakeholders (e.g., department managers) on a daily, weekly, or monthly cadence.

questionText: Are there fees for using AWS Cost Explorer or AWS Budgets?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Cost Explorer is free to access via the console; your first 2 budgets in AWS Budgets are free ($0.02 per day per active budget thereafter)

options.label: B
options.text: Both tools cost $1,000 per month flat fee

options.label: C
options.text: Cost Explorer costs $50 per click in the UI

options.label: D
options.text: Both services are strictly prohibited on free tier accounts

explanation: Accessing the AWS Cost Explorer UI is completely free. With AWS Budgets, your first two action-enabled budgets are completely free, and each additional active budget costs just $0.02 per day (about $0.60 per month).

questionText: What is AWS Organizations?

options.label: A
options.text: An account management service that enables you to consolidate multiple AWS accounts into an organization that you centrally manage and govern

options.label: B
options.text: A labor union representing cloud engineers

options.label: C
options.text: A public directory of Fortune 500 companies

options.label: D
options.text: A charity foundation run by AWS

explanation: AWS Organizations helps you centrally manage and govern your environment as you grow and scale your AWS resources. It provides consolidated billing, access control, compliance policies, and automated account provisioning.

questionText: What is Consolidated Billing in AWS Organizations?

options.label: A
options.text: A billing feature that combines the usage and charges of all member accounts into a single monthly bill paid by the management account

options.label: B
options.text: A feature that divides an invoice into 12 equal monthly installments

options.label: C
options.text: A policy that deletes invoices after payment

options.label: D
options.text: A tool that converts AWS bills into foreign currencies

explanation: Consolidated billing aggregates the charges from all member accounts in an organization onto one single, consolidated monthly bill that is paid by the primary management account.

questionText: What financial benefit does Consolidated Billing provide when multiple member accounts store large amounts of data in Amazon S3?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 volume tiering aggregates storage across all linked accounts, allowing the organization to reach cheaper per-GB tiers faster

options.label: B
options.text: S3 becomes 100% free for all member accounts

options.label: C
options.text: AWS refunds 50% of the S3 cost at the end of each year

options.label: D
options.text: S3 data is automatically mirrored to competitor cloud providers

explanation: Consolidated billing combines the storage usage of all accounts in the organization. This allows the combined usage to qualify for higher-volume discount tiers on services like Amazon S3 and data transfer faster than individual accounts could alone.

questionText: Can Reserved Instances and Savings Plans purchased by one account in an organization share discounts with other member accounts?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, RI and Savings Plans discount sharing is enabled across accounts in consolidated billing by default (unless explicitly turned off)

options.label: B
options.text: No, discounts are strictly locked to the specific account that purchased them

options.label: C
options.text: Only if both accounts have root passwords shared

options.label: D
options.text: Only between accounts in different AWS Regions

explanation: By default, the cost benefits of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are shared across all linked accounts in an AWS Organization, maximizing utilization and ensuring excess reserved capacity isn't wasted.

questionText: What is the role of the Management Account (formerly Master Account) in AWS Organizations?

options.label: A
options.text: The central administrative account that creates the organization, invites member accounts, pays the consolidated bill, and manages policies

options.label: B
options.text: A temporary account deleted after 30 days

options.label: C
options.text: An account used exclusively by third-party auditors

options.label: D
options.text: A public account accessible to anyone on the Internet

explanation: The management account is the primary account that owns the organization. It pays the consolidated monthly bill, creates or invites member accounts, and manages organizational policies like Service Control Policies (SCPs).

questionText: What are Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations?

options.label: A
options.text: Organization policies used to specify the maximum permissions boundary for member accounts and Organizational Units (OUs)

options.label: B
options.text: Scripts that automatically restart failed EC2 instances

options.label: C
options.text: Corporate code-of-conduct guidelines for remote employees

options.label: D
options.text: DNS routing rules configured in Amazon Route 53

explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) are JSON policy documents that define the maximum permissions that can be granted to IAM identities within member accounts or Organizational Units (OUs) in an organization.

questionText: Do Service Control Policies (SCPs) grant permissions to users or roles by themselves?

options.label: A
options.text: No, SCPs only set guardrails (filters) on maximum allowed permissions; an IAM policy inside the account must still grant permissions

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, attaching an SCP gives full administrative permissions automatically

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, SCPs replace the need for IAM policies entirely

options.label: D
options.text: Only when applied to the root account

explanation: SCPs act as guardrails or filters. They never grant permissions on their own; they only specify the maximum permissions available. An IAM policy attached to a user or role inside the account is still required to grant actual access.

questionText: Can a Service Control Policy (SCP) restrict actions taken by the Management Account of an AWS Organization?

options.label: A
options.text: No, SCPs do not apply to the Management Account; they only apply to member accounts and Organizational Units

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, SCPs apply equally to the Management Account and all member accounts

options.label: C
options.text: Only if the root password has 20 characters

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, if configured by AWS Support

explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) do NOT affect users or roles in the management account. They apply only to member accounts in the organization, which is why production workloads should never run in the management account.

questionText: Which capability in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console allows administrators to view and manage tax registration numbers (TRN) centrally across all linked accounts in an organization?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Tax Settings

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Artifact

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

options.label: D
options.text: AWS License Manager

questionText: Which AWS service works with AWS Organizations to centrally govern, set up, and enforce security and compliance standards across a multi-account environment using predefined landing zones?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Control Tower

options.label: B
options.text: AWS CodePipeline

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch

questionText: How does Consolidated Billing handle multiple member accounts that each have a separate AWS Free Tier allowance?

options.label: A
options.text: Free Tier limits are shared across the organization as if all accounts were a single account (meaning only one 750-hour EC2 allowance for the organization)

options.label: B
options.text: Every member account receives an independent free tier allowance that stacks multiplicatively

options.label: C
options.text: Free Tier is completely disabled when consolidated billing is activated

options.label: D
options.text: Member accounts are charged double standard rates

explanation: For billing purposes, AWS treats all accounts in an organization as if they were a single account. Therefore, free tier limits (e.g., 750 hours/month of EC2 micro instances) apply once across the entire organization, not per member account.

questionText: Which service enables you to securely share AWS resources (such as VPC subnets, Transit Gateways, and Route 53 Resolver rules) across accounts in your AWS Organization?

options.label: A
options.text: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM)

options.label: B
options.text: AWS Systems Manager

options.label: C
options.text: AWS Direct Connect

options.label: D
options.text: Amazon Simple Queue Service

explanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) helps you securely share your resources across AWS accounts, within your organization or organizational units (OUs), eliminating the need to create duplicate resources in multiple accounts.

questionText: What is the recommended best practice regarding running production application workloads in the AWS Organizations Management Account?

options.label: A
options.text: Do not run production workloads in the management account; isolate them in dedicated member accounts

options.label: B
options.text: Run all corporate workloads exclusively in the management account for ease of access

options.label: C
options.text: Share the management account root credentials with all contractors

options.label: D
options.text: Disable MFA on the management account

explanation: AWS strongly recommends using the management account solely for administrative, governance, and billing functions. Workloads should always be separated into dedicated member accounts to limit blast radius and maintain security guardrails.

questionText: What are the four primary tiers of AWS Support available to customers?

options.label: A

questionText: Which features are included with the Basic Support plan that is provided to all AWS customers at no additional cost? (Select TWO)

options.text: Phone and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers for technical architecture advice

questionText: Which is the lowest AWS Support plan that provides access to Cloud Support Engineers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week via phone, chat, and email?

options.text: Business Support Plan

options.text: Developer Support Plan

questionText: Which AWS Support plan provides business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates for 1 primary contact?

options.text: Developer Support Plan

options.text: Basic Support Plan

options.label: C
options.text: Enterprise Support Plan

questionText: Which AWS Support plan includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) who provides proactive architectural reviews and ongoing operational guidance?

options.text: Business Support Plan

questionText: What is the response time for a 'Production system down' case under the AWS Business Support plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Less than 1 hour

options.text: Less than 15 minutes

options.label: C

questionText: What is the response time target for a 'Business-critical system down' case under the Enterprise Support plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Less than 15 minutes

options.label: B
options.text: Less than 1 hour

options.label: C
options.text: Less than 30 minutes

questionText: Which team included with Enterprise Support assists customers with billing, invoice inquiries, and account management best practices?

options.label: A

questionText: What is AWS Infrastructure Event Management (IEM)?

options.label: A
options.text: A structured program that provides architectural guidance and real-time operational support during critical planned events like product launches or marketing promotions

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.text: An insurance policy reimbursing lost e-commerce revenue

explanation: Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) is a short-term engagement offering architectural reviews, capacity planning, and real-time support during planned high-profile events (e.g., product launches, Black Friday sales). Included with Enterprise Support.

questionText: What is AWS Trusted Advisor?

options.label: A
options.text: An automated online tool that analyzes your AWS environment and provides real-time recommendations across five pillars to help follow AWS best practices

options.label: B
options.text: A legal advisor hired to draft corporate contracts

options.label: C
options.text: A personal career mentor assigned to junior cloud developers

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware tester evaluating server motherboards

explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor is an online tool that acts like your customized cloud advisor, inspecting your AWS environment and making recommendations to help reduce costs, increase performance, improve security, and monitor service quotas.

questionText: What are the five core pillars evaluated by AWS Trusted Advisor?

options.label: A
options.text: Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits (Service Quotas)

options.label: B
options.text: Compute, Storage, Database, Networking, and Analytics

options.label: C
options.text: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, and SQL

options.label: D
options.text: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Durability, and Velocity

explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates your AWS infrastructure against five core categories: 1) Cost Optimization, 2) Performance, 3) Security, 4) Fault Tolerance, and 5) Service Limits (Service Quotas).

questionText: Which AWS Support plans grant access to the FULL suite of AWS Trusted Advisor checks?

options.label: A
options.text: Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, and Enterprise Support plans

options.label: B
options.text: Basic and Developer Support plans only

options.label: C
options.text: Developer Support only

options.label: D
options.text: Full checks are unavailable to any commercial customer

explanation: Customers with Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, or Enterprise Support plans receive access to all AWS Trusted Advisor checks. Basic and Developer plans have access only to 7 core security and service limit checks.

questionText: What color indicators are used in the AWS Trusted Advisor dashboard to signify check status?

options.label: A
options.text: Green (no problem detected), Yellow (investigation recommended), and Red (action recommended)

options.label: B
options.text: Blue, Purple, and Orange

options.label: C
options.text: Black, White, and Grey

options.label: D
options.text: Gold, Silver, and Bronze

explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor uses standard color indicators: Green checkmark (OK, no problem detected), Yellow exclamation (investigation recommended), and Red exclamation (action recommended to resolve a potential risk).

questionText: Which recommendation would be categorized under the 'Cost Optimization' pillar in AWS Trusted Advisor?

options.label: A
options.text: Unassociated Elastic IP addresses and idle EC2 instances

options.label: B
options.text: MFA not enabled on the root account

options.label: C
options.text: EBS volume IOPS saturation

options.label: D
options.text: Service limit nearing 80% capacity

explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar inspects for resource waste, such as unattached Elastic IP addresses (which incur charges when idle), idle Amazon RDS instances, underutilized EC2 instances, and unattached EBS volumes.

questionText: Which recommendation would be categorized under the 'Security' pillar in AWS Trusted Advisor?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon S3 bucket permissions that allow unrestricted public read/write access

options.label: B
options.text: EC2 instance CPU utilization below 10%

options.label: C
options.text: EBS snapshots older than 30 days

options.label: D
options.text: VPC peering connections with low throughput

explanation: The Security pillar alerts you to security vulnerabilities, including S3 buckets with open public access, unrestricted security group ports (0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 or 3389), and missing MFA on the root account.

questionText: What is the AWS Health Dashboard?

options.label: A
options.text: A tool providing relevant and timely information about the health of AWS services that are directly impacting your specific account resources

options.label: B
options.text: A health insurance calculator for tech workers

options.label: C
options.text: A pedometer app tracking steps taken by server engineers

options.label: D
options.text: An automated scanner for office building air quality

explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard gives you personalized visibility into the performance and availability of the AWS services you are using, showing scheduled maintenance notifications and active service incidents affecting your resources.

questionText: Which AWS Support plan provides access to consultative architectural reviews such as Well-Architected Reviews conducted by AWS Solutions Architects?

options.label: A
options.text: Enterprise Support Plan

options.label: B
options.text: Developer Support Plan

options.label: C
options.text: Basic Support Plan

options.label: D
options.text: Trial Support Plan

explanation: Enterprise Support includes proactive consultative architectural reviews, operational health checks, and Well-Architected framework reviews led by your designated Technical Account Manager (TAM).

questionText: What is the AWS Marketplace?

options.label: A
options.text: A curated digital catalog of thousands of third-party software products from Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) that run natively on AWS

options.label: B
options.text: An online grocery delivery store run by Amazon Fresh

options.label: C
options.text: A consumer flea market for used computer monitors

options.label: D
options.text: An auction site for bidding on domain names

explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated digital catalog with thousands of software listings from independent software vendors (ISVs), making it easy to find, test, buy, and deploy software (AMIs, SaaS, containers) that runs on AWS.

questionText: How does billing work for third-party software purchased through the AWS Marketplace?

options.label: A
options.text: Software licensing fees are consolidated directly onto your regular monthly AWS billing invoice

options.label: B
options.text: You must mail physical paper checks directly to the software vendor's headquarters

options.label: C
options.text: Third-party software cannot be billed on AWS

options.label: D
options.text: Billing is only processed through cryptocurrency escrow accounts

explanation: AWS Marketplace simplifies software procurement by consolidating software charges onto your regular monthly AWS bill, allowing you to pay using your existing AWS payment terms and contracts.

questionText: Which licensing models are supported for software products deployed through the AWS Marketplace? (Select TWO)

options.label: A
options.text: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) to leverage existing enterprise software investments

options.label: B
options.text: Pay-as-you-go hourly or annual subscriptions billed through AWS

options.label: C
options.text: Compulsory 99-year irrevocable land lease contracts

options.label: D
options.text: Barter exchange of consumer electronics

options.label: E
options.text: Unlicensed peer-to-peer torrent sharing

explanation: AWS Marketplace supports flexible consumption models including Pay-as-you-go (hourly, monthly, or annual subscriptions) and Bring Your Own License (BYOL) where you reuse your pre-existing software licenses in AWS.

questionText: What is AWS Service Quotas (formerly Service Limits)?

options.label: A
options.text: An AWS service that enables you to view and manage your resource usage quotas (service limits) across AWS services from a central location

options.label: B
options.text: A government trade quota on imported semiconductors

options.label: C
options.text: A monthly limit on the number of emails an employee can send

options.label: D
options.text: A restriction on the number of coffee cups allowed in server rooms

explanation: AWS Service Quotas allows you to view and manage your default resource quotas (such as maximum number of VPCs per Region or EC2 vCPUs) from a central console, and request quota increases programmatically or with a few clicks.

questionText: How can an administrator increase an adjustable service quota (such as the number of VPCs allowed in an AWS Region from 5 to 10)?

options.label: A
options.text: Submit a quota increase request via the AWS Service Quotas console or AWS Support

options.label: B
options.text: Create a second root user account inside the same VPC

options.label: C
options.text: Reboot the AWS management console web browser tab

options.label: D
options.text: Service quotas are physically hardwired and cannot be increased under any circumstances

explanation: Adjustable service quotas can be easily increased by requesting an increase via the AWS Service Quotas console or by opening a service limit increase case with AWS Support. Requests are reviewed and typically approved quickly.
